Program Leadership and Delivery

Lead and manage multiple manufacturing OT and business IT programs from initiation through completion
Take ownership of program outcomes and ensure work remains aligned with operational and business objectives
Coordinate cross-functional teams, including production, engineering, quality, supply chain, technology, and other business functions
Support new product launches, process-improvement initiatives, capital projects, and technology implementations
Ensure programs are completed on time, within scope, and according to established quality expectations
Effectively prioritize multiple projects and competing requirements in a fast-paced manufacturing environment
Promote a culture of accountability, continuous improvement, safety, quality, and operational efficiency

Program Planning and Administration

Define program objectives, scope, deliverables, milestones, dependencies, and success criteria
Develop and maintain project schedules, budgets, resource plans, and implementation roadmaps
Coordinate program resources and activities across internal teams and external stakeholders
Maintain accurate program documentation, action items, decisions, schedules, and supporting materials
Facilitate program meetings, reviews, planning sessions, and stakeholder discussions
Assist with standardizing program-management processes, tools, documentation, and best practices

Performance and Risk Management

Monitor program performance and provide regular status updates to leadership and key stakeholders
Track key performance indicators, milestones, budgets, resource utilization, and other program metrics
Identify program risks, issues, constraints, and dependencies
Develop and implement mitigation and corrective-action plans to keep programs on track
Analyze performance information to identify opportunities for improved efficiency, quality, delivery, and cost management
Escalate significant risks and issues appropriately and provide recommendations for resolution

Maintain clear and consistent communication with internal teams, leadership, and external stakeholders
Promote alignment, accountability, and transparency throughout the program lifecycle
Build and maintain effective working relationships across departments
Facilitate communication among technical teams, operational teams, business stakeholders, and leadership
Communicate complex program information clearly to technical and non-technical audiences

Lead and support continuous-improvement initiatives that increase efficiency, reduce waste, improve quality, and strengthen program delivery
Identify opportunities to improve manufacturing processes, production workflows, technology systems, and business practices
Support the development and standardization of processes, tools, and program-management best practices
Apply lessons learned to future programs and improvement initiatives
Support training and onboarding activities related to new programs, systems, processes, or procedures
Participate in audits, reviews, retrospectives, and other improvement activities supporting business objectives

Are you looking for an exciting job where you can put your skills and talents to work at a company you can feel proud to be a part of? Do you want a workplace that will challenge you and offer you opportunities to learn and grow? A position at Xcel Energy could be just what you’re looking for.

Position Summary

The Senior Threat Intelligence Analyst serves as the lead protective intelligence professional supporting Executive Protection, senior leadership, and critical business operations. This position is responsible for identifying, analyzing, assessing, and communicating threats to executives, company personnel, facilities, and operations by integrating open-source intelligence (OSINT), threat intelligence, behavioral threat assessment methodologies, travel risk intelligence, and protective intelligence operations. The role proactively monitors emerging threats, conducts executive risk assessments, provides protective intelligence support for executive travel and events, and develops actionable intelligence that enables informed security decisions. The Senior Threat Intelligence Analyst partners closely with Executive Protection Agents, the SOC, Cybersecurity, and external intelligence providers to identify and mitigate threats before they impact the organization.

Essential Responsibilities

Protective Intelligence & Threat Assessment

Conduct intelligence collection, analysis, and threat assessments related to executives, board members, high-profile employees, facilities, and corporate events.
Identify, evaluate, and monitor potential threats from individuals, groups, or movements that may impact executive safety or business operations.
Develop and maintain behavioral threat assessment case files and intelligence products.
Produce executive-focused intelligence reports, risk assessments, and protective intelligence briefings.
Conduct digital footprint assessments and identify online exposure risks to executives and family members.
Support workplace violence prevention initiatives through threat identification and intelligence analysis.

OSINT & Intelligence Collection

Perform advanced OSINT research across social media platforms, forums, websites, public records, dark web resources, and specialized intelligence databases.
Monitor online sentiment, protest activity, extremist movements, stalking behaviors, doxxing attempts, and other indicators of risk.
Utilize intelligence platforms, subscription services, and governmental reporting to identify emerging threats.
Develop intelligence collection plans and investigative methodologies to support ongoing threat cases.
Maintain awareness of geopolitical, criminal, cyber-enabled, and social threats that may impact executive safety or travel.

Executive Protection Support

Provide intelligence support for executive travel, events, public appearances, shareholder meetings, and other high-profile activities.
Conduct advance intelligence reviews of locations, venues, hotels, transportation routes, and event environments.
Produce pre-travel intelligence reports including country risk, crime trends, civil unrest, medical concerns, and transportation risks.
Support executive movement planning through continuous threat monitoring and real-time intelligence updates.
Work directly with Executive Protection Agents to identify, assess, and mitigate mission-specific risks.
Participate in executive protection operations during elevated threat situations when intelligence expertise is required.

Monitoring & Incident Response

Maintain continuous monitoring of threat reporting, intelligence feeds, social media, public information sources, and relevant security platforms.
Provide immediate notification and escalation of high-risk incidents affecting executives or operations.
Develop intelligence warnings, alerts, advisories, and executive bulletins.
Support crisis management and emergency response activities through intelligence gathering and situational awareness products.
Assist in post-incident investigations and intelligence lessons-learned reviews.

Program Development

Assist in the development and maturation of the Executive Protective Intelligence Program.
Establish threat indicators, intelligence requirements, and reporting standards.
Maintain intelligence databases, watchlists, and case management systems.
Develop metrics and trend analysis supporting executive security decision-making.
Evaluate emerging intelligence tools, technologies, and best practices to improve program effectiveness.

Minimum Requirements

Bachelor's degree in Intelligence Studies, Criminal Justice, Homeland Security, Security Management, International Relations, Political Science, Cyber Intelligence, or related field.
Minimum 5 years of experience in threat intelligence, protective intelligence, investigations, executive protection intelligence support, law enforcement intelligence, military intelligence, or related field.
Demonstrated experience conducting OSINT investigations and threat assessments.
Experience supporting executive protection operations, dignitary protection, protective services, or high-profile individuals.
Strong analytical writing and briefing capabilities.
Experience with social media intelligence collection and online threat investigations.
Ability to obtain and maintain required security clearances or authorizations.
Ability to travel up to 25% as business needs require.

Preferred Requirements

Master's degree in Intelligence Studies, Security Management, Homeland Security, or related discipline.
Experience in a corporate executive protection environment.
Experience working within a fusion center, intelligence center, law enforcement intelligence unit, military intelligence organization, or protective intelligence program.
Experience conducting behavioral threat assessments.
Experience supporting Fortune 500 executive protection programs.
Familiarity with utility, energy, or critical infrastructure security environments.

With over 130 years of experience and proven innovation, GE Vernova is leading a new era of energy. We are electrifying the world while working to decarbonize it. Our name reflects our mission. “GE” carries a legacy of quality and ingenuity. “Ver” signals Earth’s lush ecosystems, while “Nova” nods to a new era of lower-carbon energy we are helping to deliver.

Focused on the future, GE Vernova is accelerating the shift to reliable, affordable, and sustainable energy. We help customers power economies and deliver electricity vital to health, safety, and quality of life.

Let’s Talk About The Role

We are looking for a Senior Artificial Intelligence Program Manager to join our central Artificial Intelligence and Innovation team. The role will lead the delivery of strategic Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning programs supporting digital transformation across industrial businesses, acting as a Scrum Master for cross-functional teams and driving initiatives from Proof of Concept through deployment. The role will coordinate global teams and stakeholders, ensure alignment with business objectives and governance requirements, and drive successful delivery, adoption, and measurable business value.

Key responsibilities

Lead the planning and execution of complex Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning programs across multiple teams and geographies.
Own integrated program plans, milestones, dependencies, priorities, risks, and issues throughout the delivery lifecycle.
Act as Global Scrum Master for cross-functional teams, facilitating Agile ceremonies, maintaining healthy backlogs, and driving a strong delivery cadence.
Manage Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning initiatives from Proof of Concept through Minimum Viable Product and implementation, ensuring solutions are practical, scalable, and aligned with business needs.
Partner with data scientists, engineers, architects, business stakeholders, and external providers to drive delivery, adoption, and business value.
Apply Lean principles to reduce waste, improve processes, and increase delivery efficiency.
Ensure programs operate effectively within complex industrial environments, with a strong focus on quality, operational continuity, safety, and structured delivery.
Ensure delivery aligns with NPI / Stage-Gate governance and provide clear, value-focused reporting on progress, risks, dependencies, issues, and key performance indicators.
Act as a trusted coordination point between leadership, business teams, technical teams, and external partners, translating business requirements into actionable delivery plans.
Track delivery performance, adoption, and business impact, maintaining effective RAID management and challenging assumptions where needed.

What You’ll Bring (Basic Qualifications)

Bachelor's Degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or another STEM-related field.
Extensive experience in program management, project management office functions and Scrum Master roles, with strong capabilities in program planning, governance, dependency management, and RAID tracking.
Strong hands-on experience with Agile methodologies and proven ability to drive effective team delivery.
Extensive experience in industrial environments, such as manufacturing, energy, automotive, aerospace, or similar sectors, with a good understanding of NPI / Stage-Gate governance.
Solid understanding of Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning programs, including development, integration, deployment, and adoption.
Excellent stakeholder management, communication, facilitation, and executive reporting skills, with fluent written and spoken English.

What Will Make You Stand Out

Proven application of Lean principles to improve delivery, processes, or operational performance.
Experience working with technical teams, vendors, and business leaders on AI/ML or digital transformation initiatives within multinational industrial organizations.
Familiarity with DevOps, systems engineering, industrial data platforms, and delivery tools such as Jira, Azure DevOps, or equivalent.
Strong communication, interpersonal, analytical, and leadership skills, with experience working in multi-vendor environments.

Our Culture

Every action shapes our future. That’s why our north star is a culture of impact, where everyone is empowered to thrive and achieve.

Addressing the urgent need to build a more sustainable electric power system while improving the trajectory of climate change emissions are global priorities, and we take our responsibility seriously. That is our mission at GE Vernova: continuing to electrify to thrive and decarbonize the world We play a significant role in leading a new era of energy.

Our technology helps generate approximately twenty-five percent of the world’s electricity today, and we are working to power the rest. If we want the future of energy to be different, then join us and be the difference. Together, we are the Energy of Change!

We're determined to be the best place to grow

We believe that strong careers are built on a variety of experiences, strong connections, and continuous development. We’re committed to providing you the tools to navigate and shape a strong career journey that aligns with a healthy work-life balance. No two careers are the same, and yours should reflect your personal and professional goals. Your people leader and trusted mentors will support you through navigating your journey.

We also prioritize fair pay, performance-based rewards, and wellbeing programs for you and your family. With opportunities to move across teams and functions, your career can keep evolving while sustainability stays at the core of everything we do.

Inclusion & Diversity

We are passionate about creating an inclusive work environment. By valuing the ideas and contributions of a diverse workforce we help inspire others to grow, succeed, and raise the bar for everyone.

As an equal opportunity and affirmative action employer, GE Vernova is committed to support disadvantaged groups whilst providing equal opportunities for both GE Vernova associates and applicants alike.

Join us at GE Vernova where results can be achieved by embracing a community of belonging.

Peraton is a next-generation national security company that drives missions of consequence spanning the globe and extending to the farthest reaches of the galaxy. Each day, our employees solve the most daunting challenges that our customers face. Visit peraton.com to learn how we're keeping people around the world safe and secure.

Encompasses technical, engineering, data analytics, cyber security, management, operational, logistical, and administrative support for Bureau of Diplomatic Security, Cyber and Technology Security Directorate in three key offices/functional areas: Cyber Monitoring and Operations, Cyber Threat and Investigations, and Technology Innovation and Engineering State.

Peraton is seeking an experienced Data Analyst/Cyber Analytics
professional to support our Federal Strategic Cyber (FSC) Program within the Cyber & Intelligence Sector.

Location
: On-site in Arlington, VA
.

This is an excellent opportunity for a data professional who enjoys combining analytics, automation, visualization, and cybersecurity to solve real-world challenges in a high-impact federal environment.

CySA+, CASP+ CE, CCNP Security, CEH, CFR, CHFI, CISA, CISSP (or Associate), Cloud+, CND, GCED, GCIH, GICSP, SSCP

Minimum 2 years of coding experience (any programming language).
Minimum 2 years of experience in cybersecurity or data analytics.
Foundational cybersecurity knowledge or foundational understanding of network and host telemetry.
Experience developing dashboards and reports using Power BI, Tableau, or similar tools.
Ability to communicate analytical findings clearly to technical and non-technical audiences.
U.S. citizenship required.
Active Top Secret security clearance with the ability to obtain TS/SCI.

Preferred Qualifications:

Two (2) or more years of hands-on experience with Python or SQL.
Experience working with Python/Pandas for data transformation, automation, and analytics.
Experience supporting cybersecurity operations, threat analysis, or security monitoring.
Experience with large-scale operational or cybersecurity datasets.
Experience building automated reporting pipelines or analytics workflows.
Experience using data visualization tools to support leadership reporting and operational decision-making.
Familiarity with supervised and unsupervised machine learning concepts.

Experience with large, relational datasets and data structures

Experience troubleshooting data discrepancies and ensuring data integrity
Familiarity with ETL processes and data pipelines
Experience building recurring reports and dashboards
Strong attention to detail and data validation skills

Experience with automation tools and scheduling frameworks
Experience supporting executive-level decision-making

Job description:

Project manager - Rules Update Programme

18-month Fixed-Term Contract Role
Wellington-based role
Play a key role in keeping New Zealand’s aviation system safe, efficient, and fit for the future. 

At the Civil Aviation Authority, we don’t just keep New Zealand’s skies safe and secure, we help shape the future of aviation.

About the Role

As a Project Manager
within the Rules Update Programme (RUP), you'll play a critical role in delivering projects that support the modernisation of New Zealand's aviation regulatory framework. Working across multidisciplinary teams, you'll coordinate, plan and deliver complex policy and rulemaking projects that contribute to regulatory modernisation, international alignment, and positive outcomes for the aviation sector.
Reporting to the Manager, Project Delivery and Portfolio Management, you'll work closely with project leads, subject matter experts, senior stakeholders and programme governance groups to ensure projects are delivered successfully and achieve programme objectives.

Key Responsibilities 

Lead the planning, coordination, delivery and close-out of allocated Rules Update Programme projects.
Develop and maintain project schedules, plans, risks, issues and reporting.
Facilitate planning workshops and support project teams to deliver key milestones.
Engage with managers and stakeholders to secure project resources and subject matter expertise.
Provide guidance and support to project leads and project teams on project processes and delivery requirements.
Monitor project progress, manage risks and issues, and escalate matters where required.
Support stakeholder engagement and communication activities across allocated projects.
Contribute to continuous improvement activities and lessons learned processes across the programme. 

The salary range for this role is $115,536 to $141,751
. Starting salaries are based on knowledge, skills and experience the successful candidate brings to the role, as well as internal relativities. 
For more information on the role please view the position description. 

What You'll Bring 

You'll be an organised and proactive project professional who enjoys working in complex environments and coordinating diverse groups toward a common outcome. You'll be confident managing priorities, building relationships and keeping projects on track while adapting to changing requirements.

To succeed in this role you'll demonstrate: 
At least three years' experience in project management within a complex and changing operating environments.
Strong planning and organisational skills, including experience developing project schedules and plans.
Experience leading project workstreams or coordinating project teams to deliver results.
Excellent stakeholder engagement and relationship management skills.
Experience monitoring project progress, managing risks and resolving issues.
Strong analytical and problem-solving capability.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
Confidence using project management methodologies, tools and techniques.
Advanced Microsoft Office skills, including Planner, Word, Excel and PowerPoint.
Experience in the aviation sector is preferred, but not essential. 

About Us 

The Civil Aviation Authority (CAA) is New Zealand’s aviation safety and security regulator. We play a critical role in protecting the travelling public, supporting the aviation sector, and strengthening New Zealand’s international reputation. 
Our vision is simple and powerful: A safe and secure aviation system – so people are safe, and feel safe when they fly. 
Our values -  Professionalism, Respect, Integrity, Transparency, and Collaboration
 - guide everything we do. We’re committed to fostering a diverse, inclusive, and supportive environment where everyone feels respected, safe, and valued. Our people are central to our success. 

Why Join Us? 

5 weeks annual leave.
10 days sick leave, available after 6-months of continuous employment. 

Matching KiwiSaver contributions up to 4% 

Flu vaccinations 

Employee Assistance Programme 

Ready to Apply? 

This is a rare opportunity to contribute to one of the CAA’s most significant regulatory programmes of work. If you're passionate about policy, regulation, and helping create a safer, future-ready aviation system for New Zealand, we'd love to hear from you. This role is offered as an 18-month fixed term contract. 

Apply directly by completing the online application form and submitting your CV and cover letter. Your cover letter will be a key part of our assessment process, so please highlight how your experience aligns with the requirements of this role. 

We want to ensure accessibility needs are well supported, so the recruitment process is fair and equitable for all. Please let us know if there is any support we can provide to ensure the recruitment process is fully accessible to you. 

For more information, please view the position description. If you have any questions about the role or application process, contact the Recruitment team at recruitment@caa.govt.nz.

Description

The Americas DSP organization partners with entrepreneurial individuals who manage their own delivery businesses (DSPs) across the US, Canada, Brazil, and Mexico. Together, we build sustainable and scalable delivery capacity so that Amazon can continue to delight customers with fast, efficient, and bar raising fulfillment of their orders. Our North Star goal is to improve DSP Quality and help them scale their business. Quality partners operate safely and reliably, meet performance standards, take a long-term view of their business relationship with Amazon as they engage with the program, adhere to program policies, and manage healthy businesses. Within the Americas DSP organization, the DSP Shared Services team drives scalable solutions for our DSP and internal partners. We standardize complex tasks for a team of Account Managers to execute with quality.

We are seeking a Senior Program Manager to lead and drive learning and development programs that support both Delivery Service Partners (DSPs) and Business Coaches (BCs) within Amazon's Last Mile organization. This role sits at the intersection of program management, instructional strategy, and operational excellence — ensuring that DSPs and BCs have the knowledge, tools, and resources they need to deliver world-class performance. This role will also help define new workflows for our Account Management team, with a North Star of centralizing operational support for DSP owners.

Key job responsibilities

Program Strategy & Roadmap: Own the end-to-end learning program strategy for DSP and BC audiences, aligning with organizational goals around safety, quality, compliance, and operational performance
Curriculum Development & Governance: Partner with subject matter experts, instructional designers, and operations leaders to develop, maintain, and continuously improve learning content for DSP owners, drivers, and Business Coaches
Account Management Role Standardization: Define and codify the Business Coach and DSS Account Manager role — including standard operating procedures, expectations, competency frameworks, and performance benchmarks — to ensure consistency and clarity across all regions
Stakeholder Management: Serve as the central point of contact across cross-functional teams (Operations, Safety, Fleet, Compliance, Technology) to identify learning needs, prioritize initiatives, and drive alignment
Program Execution: Define project plans, manage timelines, remove blockers, and deliver programs on time and at scale across multiple regions
Metrics & Impact Measurement: Establish KPIs and success metrics for learning programs; use data to measure effectiveness, identify gaps, and drive continuous improvement
Change Management: Lead change management efforts for new program launches, policy updates, and process changes that impact DSP and BC populations
Scalability & Innovation: Identify opportunities to leverage technology, automation, and new delivery modalities (e.g., eLearning, microlearning, just-in-time resources) to scale learning programs efficiently

Basic Qualifications

5+ years of program or project management experience
Experience using data and metrics to determine and drive improvements
Experience owning program strategy, end to end delivery, and communicating results to senior leadership
Experience implementing repeatable processes and driving automation or standardization
Experience leading complex global or country-wide initiatives
Travel up to 15% of the time

Preferred Qualifications

2+ years of driving process improvements experience
Master's degree, or MBA in business, operations, human resources, adult education, organizational development, instructional design or related field
Knowledge of large scale automation and workflow management or equivalent

new_jobs.description:
Title

Program Manager (Contingency)

Belong, Connect, Grow, with KBR!

Program Summary

KBR’s Exploration & Logistics (E&L) business unit delivers mission-critical solutions supporting global defense, federal civilian, logistics, engineering, and space exploration missions. E&L provides integrated capabilities across logistics and sustainment, mission operations, engineering services, readiness and modernization programs, scientific research support, and exploration initiatives in some of the world’s most complex and challenging environments.

The business unit supports customers across the Department of Defense, federal civilian agencies, and commercial partners, delivering innovative solutions that enhance mission readiness, operational effectiveness, and long-term mission success.

Job Summary

The Program Manager (PM) serves as the single point of accountability and primary interface between KBR and the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) for all contract performance under the Public Assistance Technical Assistance Contract (PA TAC VI). The PM provides executive leadership, strategic direction, operational oversight, and quality management to ensure the successful delivery of technical, programmatic, and administrative support services in support of FEMA's Public Assistance Program and disaster recovery mission.

The PM is responsible for planning, organizing, directing, coordinating, and controlling all contract activities, resources, personnel, subcontractors, and deliverables while ensuring compliance with contract requirements, FEMA policies, federal regulations, and applicable performance standards. The PM leads a geographically dispersed workforce capable of supporting multiple concurrent disasters nationwide and ensures rapid mobilization, scalable operations, and continuous mission readiness. This position requires the ability to support nationwide disaster operations, including periodic travel and availability during emergency activation periods. In addition, Direct day-to-day contract execution across all task orders and disaster assignments and managing nationwide surge operations and disaster deployment activities which includes: coordinating staffing, resource allocation, and workload balancing to support multiple simultaneous disaster operations. While ensuring timely mobilization, deployment, tracking, and demobilization of personnel, the PM must have sound PM skills and capabilities demonstrated by supporting other FEMA programs or similar complex programs.

The PM will ensure contract performance meets or exceeds all performance metrics, service level requirements, and quality standards and leads program governance activities, including executive reviews, performance assessments, risk management, and continuous improvement initiatives. While maintaining responsibility for overall contract cost, schedule, and performance.

Please Note:
This role is contingent upon final project approval and contract funding.

Core Competencies

Strategic Leadership
Federal Program Management
FEMA Public Assistance Expertise
Disaster Recovery Operations
Stakeholder Management
Quality Assurance and Continuous Improvement
Risk Management
Resource Planning and Workforce Management
Financial and Contract Management
Executive Communication
Problem Solving and Decision Making
Mission-Focused Service Delivery

The Program Manager Shall Demonstrate

Comprehensive knowledge of FEMA Public Assistance Program delivery, grant management, and disaster recovery operations.
Experience applying Stafford Act authorities, 2 CFR Part 200, FEMA Public Assistance Program and Policy Guide (PAPPG), and applicable federal regulations.
Experience managing large-scale disaster recovery operations involving multiple simultaneous federally declared disasters.
Training and experience in Incident Command System (ICS) principles and emergency management operations.
Experience overseeing geographically dispersed teams supporting field, regional, and headquarters operations.
Familiarity with FEMA's recovery mission, state and local government coordination, and stakeholder engagement processes.

This role requires an experienced, forward-leaning leader capable of operating in austere, rapidly changing environments while maintaining strict compliance with contractual, safety, and quality standards. The PM will enforce KBR’s Zero Harm culture and ensure all operations are executed in accordance with company policies, applicable regulations, and customer requirements

Roles And Responsibilities

Lead the contract and task orders with day-to-day execution of program operations, ensuring sustainment goals, strategic objectives, financial goals, and customer expectations are met or exceeded.
Liaison between key stakeholders to ensure efficient delivery and proactive risk management.
Plan and support execution of End-Use Monitoring (EUM) activities, including in-person, secondary, and virtual monitoring inspections in Ukraine.
Design and implement monitoring tools and program surveys, including sampling plans, tool development, and digital data collection methods.
Lead field supervision efforts to generate high-quality evidence on program performance and outcomes.
Oversee data cleaning, validation, and analysis to ensure structure, accuracy, integrity, and readiness for internal decision-making and external reporting.
Prepare clear, funder-ready analytical reports and professional data visualizations that translate complex findings into actionable insights and demonstrate results against agreed indicators and targets.
Oversee and manage a team of contractor personnel technically proficient in monitoring and evaluation activities and possess the requisite property management and related experience necessary for EUM.

Description

The Senior Operations Program Manager (OPM) is responsible for aligning all resources needed to support assigned programs at the DFW11 facility in Dallas, TX from Postponement Approval through End of Life. The OPM coordinates planning, material management, site technical, and Contract Manufacturer (CM) resources to deliver factory readiness, production launch, and sustained operations on time and on budget. The OPM partners with Site Technical Managers and Sunnyvale Product Managers to plan new product introductions, and drives cross-functional execution with Engineering, Quality, Automation, and the CM across every phase of the program lifecycle.

Key job responsibilities

Own all aspects of factory readiness from project kick-off through production launch and sustained operations.
Represent DPO to the Operations and Supply Chain Organization for each assigned program.
Create and manage detailed program schedules to drive readiness for all site build-out, fit-up, and factory deliverables.
Manage, track, report, and forecast all costs for site build-out, fit-up, and factory deliverables.
Identify and escalate risks in manufacturing process development, equipment delivery, quality control plans, and validation schedules.
Oversee the Contract Manufacturer's coordination of contractors and suppliers for installation and maintenance of power and data infrastructure, compressed air services, and other site equipment.
Lead or participate in daily standup meetings during program launches, control runs, and line installations.
Drive operational improvements using Lean and 6σ practices.
Report on program metrics and goals on a monthly basis to all levels of the organization.
Travel as needed to accomplish business needs.
Drive the Contract Manufacturer (CM) to meet production, quality, cost, and schedule targets through regular performance reviews, metric tracking, and escalation when goals are at risk.
Own Engineering Change Order (ECO) management for assigned programs, including receiving change notifications, assessing factory impact, ensuring production compliance, and informing the Materials Manager and Sr. Planner of BOM, process, and schedule implications.

A day in the life

The OPM is actively engaged in aligning resources and driving program execution at DFW11 across every stage from Postponement Approval through End of Life. On any given day, the OPM may be working with STMs and Sunnyvale Product Managers to plan capacity, material, and technology requirements for a new product introduction, defining manufacturing strategies and site readiness requirements for a project launch, or leading the daily standup during a production ramp to drive issue resolution and report progress against yield targets. During sustained operations, the OPM focuses on operational improvements and CM performance management. Amazon's Lab126 began in 2004 as a subsidiary of Amazon.com, Inc., originally creating the best-selling Kindle family of products. new_jobs.description:
At Team Global Express, we're transforming the future of logistics through data, artificial intelligence, automation and integration. We're seeking an experienced Lead Business Analyst to play a key role in shaping innovative solutions that improve customer experiences, operational performance and commercial outcomes across our business.

This is an exciting opportunity to lead a team of Business Analysts while partnering with senior stakeholders to identify, prioritise and deliver strategic initiatives that create real business value.

About The Role

As the Lead Business Analyst - Data, AI & Integration, you will act as the bridge between business leaders and technology teams, translating opportunities and challenges into scalable, data-driven solutions.

You'll provide leadership across business analysis activities, guide discovery and solution design, and help shape the roadmap for data, AI, automation and integration initiatives. Working closely with stakeholders across the organisation, you'll ensure solutions are aligned to strategic priorities and support sustainable business growth.

What You'll Do

Lead, coach and develop other Business Analysts, ensuring high-quality analysis and delivery outcomes.
Partner with business leaders to identify opportunities for data, AI, automation and process improvement.
Facilitate workshops to gather requirements, define business problems and develop solution options.
Lead current-state and future-state process analysis and documentation activities.
Identify and assess AI and automation opportunities, including business value, risks and operational readiness.
Translate business requirements into epics, user stories, acceptance criteria and delivery-ready artefacts.
Collaborate with Architecture, Delivery, Data, AI and Integration teams to design practical and scalable solutions.
Manage competing priorities and BA resources across strategic projects, operational initiatives and business-as-usual activities.
Champion continuous improvement and uplift business analysis practices across the function.
Act as a trusted advisor to stakeholders exploring new technologies and ways of working.

What You'll Bring

Significant experience leading business analysis activities within complex technology, digital, data or transformation environments.
Demonstrated experience managing Business Analysts and coordinating work across multiple initiatives.
Strong stakeholder engagement and relationship management skills, with the ability to influence at all levels.
Expertise in requirements gathering, process mapping, business process improvement and solution design.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to translate complex business problems into practical outcomes.
Excellent communication, facilitation and workshop leadership capabilities.
Experience working in Agile, Waterfall or hybrid delivery environments.
A continuous improvement mindset and a passion for delivering measurable business value.
An understanding of project financials
Lean Six Sigma certification - nice to have

About Team Global Express

Team Global Express (TGE) is an Australian-owned transport and logistics business delivering to Australia and New Zealand. We’re not only transforming our operations but striving towards changing the logistics industry and becoming an Environmental, Social, and Governance leader by 2030. To learn more about our story, visit https://teamglobalexp.com/.

Why TGE

We care about our customers, our people, and our planet. We are always innovating and improving our services. We are driven by passion and purpose, and we never stop.

What We Offer

Competitive salary above industry standards
Upskilling, training, mentoring and more to support your career development journey
Fun and practical employee perks and discounts
Flexible work, including work from home
Inclusive parental leave policy that supports all parents & carers

new_jobs.title: HR Operations Project Manager
new_jobs.description:
At Lyft, our purpose is to serve and connect. We aim to achieve this by cultivating a work environment where all team members belong and have the opportunity to thrive.

We are looking for a Senior Program Manager – HR Operations to drive operational excellence, process optimization, and scalable innovation. Sitting directly within HR Operations, this role serves as a key operational engine for modernizing how we work—focusing on business process design, seamless M&A operational readiness, and modern tool enablement (including practical AI and automation).

In this role, you will partner closely with our Corporate Engineering & IT team (CEIT), as well as cross-functional leaders in Team Member Experience, M&A, Talent Acquisition, Total Rewards, Legal, and IT. Your focus will be on bridging business strategy with operational delivery: evaluating workflows, streamlining integrations, and driving organizational change and adoption with greater speed and efficiency.

The ideal candidate is both a seasoned project manager and an operational innovator. You deeply understand core HR business processes, know how to integrate acquired teams smoothly, and can partner with technical leads to pilot, launch, and scale workflows that enhance the employee experience.

Success in this role will be measured by:
The efficiency, quality, and adoption of HR operational solutions delivered—including reduced SLA turnaround times, smooth integration of acquired operational processes, elimination of manual friction, improved employee CSAT, and increased capability across the People organization.

Responsibilities:

HR Process Optimization

Identify & Streamline High-Impact Workflows: Evaluate end-to-end HR processes across the employee lifecycle to eliminate friction, improve accuracy, and incorporate automation where appropriate.
Translate Business Needs for Technical counterparts: Map out clear "as-is" and "to-be" operational processes and success metrics, allowing technical and engineering partners to convert them into actionable specs.
Serve as an HR Operations Advisor: Help HR functional leads understand operational best practices, evaluate current state bottlenecks, and identify practical opportunities for process redesign and technology enablement.

M&A Integration & Operational Readiness

Lead HR Ops M&A Execution: Partner with cross-functional M&A leads to assess incoming HR systems, policies, and operational processes during corporate transactions.
Harmonize & Consolidate: harmonize acquired employee workflows into Lyft's core HR Operations service delivery model with minimal business disruption.
Change & Onboarding Support: Oversee operational readiness plans to ensure acquired employees transition smoothly into Lyft’s HR tools, service desks, and operational standards.

Technical Partnership & Tool Delivery

Liaison to CEIT & Solution Architecture: Partner hand-in-hand with the AI Business Solution Architect (PeopleTech) and IT teams to co-design, validate, and launch HR technology solutions (including automation, and AI workflows).
Pilot & Solution Validation: Utilize light-touch automation, low-code tools, and digital platforms to prototype quick operational improvements and test solutions before full-scale deployment.
User Acceptance Testing (UAT): Lead UAT and operational readiness reviews to ensure enterprise tools built in core systems (Workday, Greenhouse, Jira, etc.) solve business needs cleanly.

Enablement, Change Management & Governance

Drive Capability & Adoption: Lead change management strategies for new HR programs, offering hands-on workshops, clear documentation, training materials, and practical "how-to" playbooks.
Embed & Support: Pair directly with HR business partners, recruiters, and ops specialists to build confidence and capability in adopting new operational workflows and technology tools.

Experience:

5+ years of Program/Project Management experience, specifically within HR Operations, HR Systems Transformation, or HR Service Delivery.
Experience with AI, HR Technology & Automation: Experience leveraging AI enabled tools and HR tech (e.g., LLMs, smart intake, automated routing) to optimize business processes.
Demonstrated M&A Experience: Hands-on experience supporting M&A activity, specifically around HR operational integration, system consolidation, and process harmonization.
Proven Technical Partnership: Track record of serving as the operational bridge between business teams and technical partners (e.g., Solution Architects, Product Managers, IT Engineers).
Cross-Functional Change Management: Demonstrated ability to drive alignment, lead complex change initiatives, and inspire tool adoption across non-technical stakeholders in a matrixed environment.
Data Privacy & Compliance Mindset: Deep appreciation for PII protection, data privacy standards, and regulatory considerations in employee operations.

Nice-to-Haves

Experience in high-growth tech environments or organizations undergoing significant operational scaling.
Deep familiarity with core People enterprise systems (e.g., Workday, Greenhouse, Jira, Slack).
Hands-on experience with business automation platforms (e.g., Workato, UiPath, Power Automate, Slack Workflows).

Benefits:

Great medical, dental, and vision insurance options with additional programs available when enrolled
Mental health benefits
Family building benefits
Child care and pet benefits
401(k) plan with company match to help save for your future
In addition to 12 observed holidays, salaried team members have discretionary paid time off, hourly team members have 15 days paid time off
18 weeks of paid parental leave. Biological, adoptive, and foster parents are all eligible
Subsidized commuter benefits
Monthly Lyft credits and complimentary Lyft Pink membership

Lyft is an equal opportunity employer committed to an inclusive workplace that fosters belonging. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regards to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability status, protected veteran status, age, genetic information, or any other basis prohibited by law. We also consider qualified applicants with criminal histories consistent with applicable federal, state and local law.

Lyft highly values having employees working in-office to foster a collaborative work environment and company culture. This role will be in-office on a hybrid schedule following the establishment of a Lyft office in Nashville — Team Members will be expected to work in the office 3 days per week on Mondays, Wednesdays, and Thursdays. Lyft considers working in the office at least 3 days per week to be an essential function of this hybrid role. Additionally, hybrid roles have the flexibility to work from anywhere for up to 4 weeks per year. #Hybrid

The expected base pay range for this position in the Nashville area is $88,560-$110,700, not inclusive of potential equity offering, bonus or benefits. Salary ranges are dependent on a variety of factors, including qualifications, experience and geographic location. Your recruiter can share more information about the salary range specific to your working location and other factors during the hiring process.

He aha te mea nui o tēnei ao? He tangata, he tangata, he tangata.

Hello, Kia ora, Noa’ia, Talofa lava, Mauri, Mālō e lelei, Tālofa, Ni Sa Bula Vinaka, Fakaalofa lahi atu, Mālō ni, Kia orana , nǐ hǎo, Kamusta.

WorkSafe New Zealand | Mahi Haumaru Aotearoa Is The Primary Workplace Health And Safety Regulator. Our Vision Is That Everyone Who Goes To Mahi Comes Home Healthy And Safe. We Live By Our Values:

Kōrero mai – we engage meaningfully

About Your Team / Ko Te Tīma

Enterprise Planning and Implementation is a new group established at WorkSafe to strengthen planning, coordination, and implementation across the organisation, particularly to improve how work is prioritised, sequenced, and supported through to delivery.

The Regulatory Intelligence team plays a critical role in helping WorkSafe make informed regulatory decisions that improve health and safety outcomes across Aotearoa. Working closely with frontline inspectors and operational leaders, the team transforms data, information, and operational insights into intelligence products and actionable insights that support targeting, prioritisation, and regulatory action.

About The Role / Ō Te Tūranga

As an Intelligence Analyst, Regional, you'll provide operational regulatory intelligence that supports frontline inspectorate activity within your region. You'll analyse data and information from a range of sources, identify emerging risks and trends, and translate your findings into clear intelligence products that help inspectors and operational leaders target their efforts where they can have the greatest impact.

Working closely with inspectors and regulatory teams, you'll help ensure WorkSafe's regulatory activities are evidence-based, targeted, and responsive to changing risks and priorities.

What You'll Do/ Ko tōu ake mahi

Analyse operational data and information to identify regional risks and emerging trends.
Develop intelligence products that support regulatory targeting and prioritisation.
Translate complex findings into practical, actionable intelligence.
Build strong relationships with inspectors and operational stakeholders to understand emerging regulatory challenges
Provide timely intelligence support for regional regulatory activities.
Produce operational reports and dashboards that support decision-making.
Escalate emerging issues requiring wider organisational attention.

What You'll Bring / Ko ngā pukenga ōu

Experience analysing quantitative and qualitative information to generate meaningful insights.
Strong critical thinking skills with the ability to work with incomplete or ambiguous information.
Proven ability to write clear, structured reports or intelligence products.
Experience managing competing priorities and stakeholder requests.
Strong relationship-building and stakeholder engagement skills.
Experience in an intelligence, regulatory, or public sector environment is desirable.
A relevant qualification, or progress towards one, in intelligence analysis or a related analytical discipline is advantageous.

Nāu te rourou, nāku te rourou, ka ora ai te iwi.

Employee-led networks to promote the goals and needs of our diverse communities (Rainbow, Pacific, Women’s and Tū Rangatira Māori Network)

Data Analyst

Position Overview

Our client is seeking a Data Analyst to play a critical role in improving the quality, reliability, and scalability of their data ecosystem. This position focuses on identifying and resolving data inconsistencies, analyzing complex datasets, and building a more reliable data foundation across operational systems.

Enterprise Planning and Implementation is a new group established at WorkSafe to strengthen planning, coordination, and implementation across the organisation, particularly to improve how work is prioritised, sequenced, and supported through to delivery.

The Regulatory Intelligence team plays a critical role in helping WorkSafe make informed regulatory decisions that improve health and safety outcomes across Aotearoa. Working closely with frontline inspectors and operational leaders, the team transforms data, information, and operational insights into intelligence products and actionable insights that support targeting, prioritisation, and regulatory action.

About The Role / Ō Te Tūranga

As an Intelligence Analyst, Regional, you'll provide operational regulatory intelligence that supports frontline inspectorate activity within your region. You'll analyse data and information from a range of sources, identify emerging risks and trends, and translate your findings into clear intelligence products that help inspectors and operational leaders target their efforts where they can have the greatest impact.

Working closely with inspectors and regulatory teams, you'll help ensure WorkSafe's regulatory activities are evidence-based, targeted, and responsive to changing risks and priorities.

Analyse operational data and information to identify regional risks and emerging trends.
Develop intelligence products that support regulatory targeting and prioritisation.
Translate complex findings into practical, actionable intelligence.

Provide timely intelligence support for regional regulatory activities.
Produce operational reports and dashboards that support decision-making.

Experience analysing quantitative and qualitative information to generate meaningful insights.

Experience managing competing priorities and stakeholder requests.
Strong relationship-building and stakeholder engagement skills.

Description

Passionate about Safety? Join our dynamic team as a Senior Contractor Safety Program Manager and make a real impact on the North America operations that power the world's largest e-commerce company!

In this exciting role, you'll be a key partner to Procurement, Field Workplace, Health, and Safety (WHS), and site support teams such as Reliability, Maintenance, and Engineering (RME), working closely with them to ensure world-class safety standards for our under the roof contractors across Amazon North America Operations. You will also liaison externally with Amazon's contractor qualification partner, Avetta, supporting product enhancements and contractor partnership.

You will be empowered to own and drive safety programs from inception through implementation.

You will also own safety related projects and own the actions needed to deliver them.

Also supporting field operations daily safety routines, you will support rigorous investigations to uncover root causes, develop actions, and share learnings.

Collaborating cross-functionally, you'll scale successful safety initiatives and improvement projects, cementing Amazon's reputation as an industry leader. If you're a motivated safety professional committed to continuous improvement, this is an unparalleled opportunity to make your mark.

Bring your safety expertise and collaborative mindset - together, we'll reinvent what's possible! Apply now.

Key job responsibilities

A successful candidate will be able to own and drive safety programs from inception through implementation.

The candidate will own safety related projects and own the actions needed to deliver them including narrative paper writing for executive leadership audiences.

Ability to assess contractor high risk operations, such as work at heights, hazardous energy, and lifting and rigging and implement strategies to minimize risk.

Serve as a trusted safety partner to senior regional leaders across North America, aligning on strategic priorities and tracking progress against goals.

Conduct regular site visits to Amazon warehouse locations to personally observe safety practices, gather feedback from frontline teams, and identify opportunities for improvement.

Utilize insights from site visits to develop and update safety standards, protocols, and training materials that drive consistent, best-in-class safety performance.

Lead comprehensive incident investigations, rapidly identify root causes, and implement corrective actions to prevent recurrence.

Collaborate cross-functionally with teams in Operations, Procurement, Construction, and beyond to scale successful safety initiatives and embed sustainable improvements.

Monitor safety metrics, analyze trends, and present recommendations to senior leadership on priorities and investment areas.

A day in the life

You might start with a series of check-in calls, connecting with Procurement and Regional Site WHS leaders across North America to discuss emerging issues, share best practices, and align on priorities. Then, you hop on a global project call, collaborating with teammates from around the world to finalize a new digital safety tool. In the afternoon, you analyze leading indicator data, identifying an opportunity for improvement.

About The Team

The North America WHS Contractor Safety team collaborates cross-functionally to develop and improve contractor safety policies, procedures, and standards. We provide SME knowledge and support for contractor safety management, deep dive performance through Avetta, and track incident data for risk-based decisions. We standardize contractor project safety documentation and under-the-roof contractor management through Avetta Worksite Safety. We drive standardized contractor competence by collecting and training records and experience via Avetta Worker Management. We ensure contractors adhere to Amazon safety requirements through orientation and acknowledgement of Special Safety Conditions.

Basic Qualifications

6+ years of program or project management experience
Experience owning program strategy, end to end delivery, and communicating results to senior leadership
Experience using data and metrics to determine and drive improvements
5+ years of increasing responsibilities in EHS or environmental programs in manufacturing, production, or service operations experience
Bachelor’s degree in engineering, safety, environmental, or equivalent field of study
Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) fluency

Preferred Qualifications

Master's degree
Knowledge of Excel at an intermediate level (e.g., pivot tables & charts, multiple criteria lookups, nested logical/IF formulas, data cleansing, array formulas, etc.)
Experience prioritizing and managing time effectively in dynamic environments
Experience solving complex problems quantitatively and develop actionable data-driven business recommendations
Experience owning the development and implementation of contractor safety programs
Associate Safety Professional (ASP), Certified Safety Professional (CSP), Project Management Professional (PMP)

SOVOS

Sales Operations Analyst

Revenue Operations·Full-Time·Chile

Build your future with Sovos.

If you're seeking a career where innovation meets impact, you've come to the right place. As a global leader, Sovos is transforming tax compliance from a business requirement to a force for growth while revolutionizing how businesses navigate the ever-changing regulatory landscape.

At Sovos, we're dedicated to more than just solving compliance challenges -- we're committed to making a positive and lasting difference in everything we do. Our teams operate on the modern edge of digital technology, working not only to solve complex business challenges but also to enrich our personal, professional, and local communities.

Our purpose-built systems provide the tools you need to thrive in a world where governments demand increased visibility, faster reporting and greater control over business processes. Excited about the possibilities? So are we!

Don't worry if you don't check all the boxes -- apply anyway! We're focused on hiring the right people, not just the "right" resume. It's not about what you've done elsewhere; it's all about what you're capable of doing here.

The Role

At Sovos, we're transforming how businesses navigate tax compliance on a global scale. As a Sales Operations Analyst, you'll partner with Sales and Marketing teams to optimize systems, streamline processes, and maintain data integrity across our go-to-market operations. This role sits at the intersection of strategy and execution, enabling our teams to work smarter while driving continuous improvement across our revenue operations.

More Specifically, You Will

Serve as the go-to-market representative for the Sales Operations team, providing direct user support on Salesforce and other critical tools that enable the sales force.
Implement and enforce processes and tools that maintain integrity and accuracy of Salesforce data, leveraging AI-assisted workflows to identify anomalies and optimize data quality.
Develop comprehensive sales analytics and management dashboards that provide actionable insights to leadership, sales teams, and cross-functional partners.
Create and maintain internal controls, system documentation, and the Sales Operations Manual to ensure consistency and knowledge sharing across the organization.
Manage ad-hoc reporting requests while serving as subject matter expert on reporting tools, methodologies, and emerging AI-powered analytics solutions.
Build strong cross-functional relationships to ensure seamless information flow across systems and departments, driving continuous improvement through proactive process optimization.
Provide sales support, training, and project coordination while accommodating user requests and ensuring both internal and external customer satisfaction.

What You Bring to Sovos

Bachelor's degree in Business Management or equivalent demonstrated experience in sales operations, analytics, or related field.
You've built solid experience in sales operations or revenue operations, with strong Salesforce proficiency.
Fluent English communication skills, both written and verbal.
Deep understanding of sales operations processes including sales cycles, CRM applications, forecasting, territory management, and quota administration.
Advanced analytical and quantitative skills with ability to identify trends, develop data-driven solutions, and comfort with AI-assisted analytics tools.
Expert-level Microsoft Excel skills and proficiency across the Microsoft suite.
Strong project management capabilities with proven training and facilitation experience, plus excellent communication and presentation skills for diverse audiences.
Comfortable working independently and taking initiative learner who works effectively both independently and collaboratively, balancing team partnership with self-directed problem-solving and handles confidential information with discretion.

Sovos is a global provider of tax, compliance and trust solutions and services that enable businesses to navigate an increasingly regulated world with true confidence. Purpose-built for always-on compliance capabilities, our scalable IT-driven solutions meet the demands of an evolving and complex global regulatory landscape. If you're looking for the stability of a profitable, growing company with the entrepreneurial spirit of a startup, we’re hiring. SageSure, a leader in catastrophe-exposed property insurance, is seeking an Program Analyst. In this role, you'll help bridge the gap between business needs and technology solutions by supporting the analysis, documentation, and continuous improvement of insurance products, processes, and systems. As a key member of the dedicated Commercial team, you'll partner with stakeholders across Product, Engineering, Quality Assurance, and Operations to gather requirements, document business processes, validate solutions, and support strategic initiatives. This role is ideal for a detail-oriented problem solver who enjoys collaborating with cross-functional teams, improving processes, and helping deliver high-quality solutions that support business growth and operational excellence.

What you’d be doing:

Partner with business, product, engineering, and operational stakeholders to gather, analyze, document, and validate business and technical requirements.
Develop and maintain clear, accurate, and comprehensive requirements documentation, process flows, user stories, and supporting artifacts.
Collaborate with engineering and solution design teams to ensure requirements are well-defined, understood, and aligned with business objectives.
Review and validate requirements with stakeholders, ensuring accuracy, completeness, and alignment across impacted teams.
Coordinate with Quality Assurance teams to support testing efforts and ensure delivered solutions meet documented business requirements.
Analyze existing systems, processes, and workflows to identify opportunities for improvement, increased efficiency, and enhanced user experiences.
Support the documentation and refinement of business processes, operational procedures, and system capabilities.
Build strong working relationships through a combination of virtual collaboration, office visits, stakeholder meetings, workshops, and in-person working sessions.
Facilitate discussions and working sessions with stakeholders across multiple functions, locations, and time zones.
Contribute to the continuous improvement of requirements management, documentation standards, and business analysis practices.
Support implementation activities, issue resolution, and post-launch follow-up as needed.
Participate in special projects and strategic initiatives that support organizational priorities.

We’re looking for someone who has:

Bachelor's degree or equivalent experience, preferably in Business, Insurance, Information Systems, Computer Science, or a related field.
1–3 years of Property & Casualty insurance experience, preferably within Commercial Insurance.
Experience gathering, documenting, analyzing, and validating business requirements.
Strong written and verbal communication skills with the ability to communicate effectively across technical and non-technical audiences.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with exceptional attention to detail.
Ability to understand complex business processes and translate them into clear, actionable requirements.
Experience working with cross-functional teams in a collaborative environment.
Familiarity with insurance policy administration, sales, servicing, or operational workflows.
Proficiency in Microsoft Excel and other business productivity tools.
Ability to work effectively in a hybrid and geographically distributed environment, leveraging both virtual and in-person collaboration.
Ability to collaborate effectively with cross-functional partners located across multiple offices and time zones.
Ability and willingness to travel periodically for team meetings, stakeholder engagement, office visits, offsites, and company events (approximately 10–15% annually).

Highly preferred candidates also have:

Experience working with Smartsheet, Confluence, Jira, or similar project and requirements management tools.
Experience reverse engineering business processes, system functionality, or requirements documentation.
Familiarity with XML, JSON, SQL, or other technical concepts used in software development environments.
Experience working within Agile development teams and methodologies.
Experience supporting insurance product implementations, enhancements, or operational transformation initiatives.

Commercial at SageSure:

At SageSure, our Commercial team is helping shape the future of one of the company's most important growth areas. We're bringing together talented professionals across product management, engineering, operations, data, and business functions to build innovative solutions, streamline processes, and create scalable capabilities that support long-term success. Whether developing new products, improving customer experiences, or solving complex business challenges, our team is focused on turning ideas into impact. Join us and be part of a collaborative, fast-moving environment where you'll have the opportunity to influence strategy, drive innovation, and help build what's next.

About SageSure:

Named among the Best Places to Work in Insurance by Business Insurance for four years in a row (2020-2023), SageSure is one of the largest managing general underwriters (MGU) focused on catastrophe-exposed property in the US. Since its founding in 2009, SageSure has experienced exceptional growth while generating underwriting profits for carrier partners through hurricanes, wildfires, and hail. You’ll translate business challenges into requirements and own the delivery of those requirements for the Revenue function.
This role is essential to the success of our SAP transformation efforts across Order to Cash and Finance.

What You’ll Do

Initiate

Attend design workshops and help disposition requirements
Help break larger work items into smaller tasks based on functionality

Provide input for acceptance criteria

Resolve issues during Go-Live support
Transition the solution to the support team

Grade: Professional 308

Job Description

Want to use your data skills to improve how thousands of students learn?

At WGU, data drives decision-making, from course design to student support. As a Data Analyst on our Learning Program Analytics team, you'll work with large-scale, high-value datasets to help evaluate what's working and what's not, so we can help every student succeed. You'll partner closely with cross-functional teams to turn complex data into clear, actionable insights using rigorous analytical methods.

What You'll Do

Analyze large datasets to uncover trends and deliver actionable insights that inform program development and student engagement strategies
Build, maintain, and enhance dashboards and data visualizations, including consolidating and improving existing reporting assets
Translate stakeholder needs into technical requirements and deliver clear, data-driven solutions
Partner with Data Engineering to support ETL and data pipeline development
Perform ad hoc analyses and communicate findings through compelling data storytelling
Identify and resolve data quality issues to ensure accuracy and reliability of insights
Apply descriptive statistics and analytical methods to identify patterns and support sound conclusions
Document methodology, sources, and insight history to support transparency and reproducibility
Understand and apply relevant data governance and security policies to access, use, and store data responsibly
Collaborate with cross-functional teams including Program Development, Product, and Decision Intelligence to support key initiatives
Build toward greater autonomy in driving tasks and small-scale projects, with growing independence in tracking progress and navigating dependencies

What You'll Bring

Bachelor's degree in a related discipline
3 years of related experience in Data Analysis, Business Intelligence, Data Science, Statistics, Decision Intelligence, Research, Learning Science, or Behavioral/Cognitive Psychology
Strong SQL skills and experience querying large datasets
Experience with Tableau or Power BI for data visualization
Experience working with ETL or ELT processes and data pipelines
Solid working knowledge of descriptive statistics and analytical methods, with the ability to apply them to real-world datasets to identify trends and support data-driven conclusions
Ability to apply sound judgment and analytical thinking to identify root causes of data issues and inform recommendations

Bonus Points

Experience working with large-scale datasets containing millions of records
Familiarity with Databricks or similar data platforms
Experience contributing to dashboard optimization or consolidation projects
Proficiency in a programming language such as Python or R
Exposure to GitHub and analytics documentation standards

What To Expect

At WGU, our mission drives everything we do, including how we hire. Our interview experience is designed to give qualified candidates the opportunity to show their best work through meaningful conversations and collaboration.

We thoughtfully review every application and invite forward the candidates whose experience and potential best align with the role and our mission.

Introductory call
Hiring manager interview
Technical interview
Interview with Sr Director

This is a full-time, in-office position requiring five days per week in our Salt Lake City, UT office, designed to foster the collaboration and connection that fuel our best work.

While we welcome applicants from all backgrounds, WGU is not able to provide visa sponsorship for this role.

This position requires occasional travel of up to 20%, including required attendance at designated company summits (typically one to two per year). Additional travel may include conferences, visits to company locations, and other business-related events as needed. Additional travel may be assigned as needed to support business requirements.

Enterprise Planning and Implementation is a new group established at WorkSafe to strengthen planning, coordination, and implementation across the organisation, particularly to improve how work is prioritised, sequenced, and supported through to delivery.

Experience analysing data and information from multiple sources to generate insights that inform organisational or operational decisions

Excellent analytical thinking and communication skills, with the ability to build trusted relationships across teams
Strong expertise in SQL coding and Power BI, with proven experience developing and maintaining impactful dashboards. Experience with Power Apps and Power Automate is preferred
Nice to have experience: Experience with Crystal Reports and/or financial reporting skills

Additional Skills Required For Senior Role:

Demonstrated experience providing leadership, guidance, or mentoring within an analytical or intelligence environment
Proven ability to influence senior decision-making through the delivery of high-impact strategic products
Strong understanding of intelligence analysis methodologies and practices in a regulatory or public sector context

Nāu te rourou, nāku te rourou, ka ora ai te iwi.

Own the live installation schedule across vendors, delivery stations, and regions — adjusting in real time for VIN availability, vendor capacity, and site constraints while ensuring zero disruption to daytime delivery operations
Manage daily VIN tracking and reconciliation across branded fleet and Last Mile Rental systems; own parts receiving, site storage, and vehicle availability at delivery stations

Manage daily DS/DSP communication across multiple channels to confirm vehicle availability and resolve scheduling conflicts
Build network rollout plans — quantities, locations, and sequencing — and own PO submissions, workback plans, and procurement alignment
Drive campaign closeout including inventory reconciliation, maintenance and repair handoff, warranty documentation, and lessons learned
Provide weekly dashboard updates on completion status, cost performance, and quality metrics to leadership

A day in the life

This role will interact with DSPs, RFMs, product owners, and vendors nearly daily to ensure success, control cost and quality.

5+ years of program or project management experience
Experience using data and metrics to determine and drive improvements
Experience owning program strategy, end to end delivery, and communicating results to senior leadership

Procon is a top-ranked construction management and technology consulting firm with 25 years of experience delivering high‑impact projects across the U.S. and worldwide. An ENR Top 100 CM/PM firm for five consecutive years, we specialize in program management, project controls, commissioning, and technology—and offer an excellent platform to grow your career while shaping the future of the built environment.

Procon seeks an experienced Project Manager to support the District of Columbia Department of General Services (DGS) and DC Public Schools (DCPS) Capital Construction Program in Washington, DC. The selected candidate will serve as the Owner's Representative, managing and supporting school modernization, renovation, capital improvement, and facility infrastructure projects throughout the full project lifecycle, including planning, procurement, design, preconstruction, construction, occupancy, closeout, and turnover. Projects may include occupied school renovations, major modernizations, additions, athletic facilities, campus improvements, and building systems upgrades.

Ideal candidates will have experience with K-12 schools, educational facilities, higher education, or public-sector capital improvement programs; however, professionals with comparable commercial, municipal, healthcare, government, transit, or institutional construction experience will also be considered. This role requires various skills and experience as listed below.

Requirements

Qualifications and Skills

Bachelor's degree in Construction Management, Engineering, Architecture, Building Construction, Project Management, or a related field.
Minimum of 5 years of construction or capital project management experience; 7+ years preferred.
Demonstrated experience managing projects through design, procurement, construction, closeout, and occupancy.
Strong knowledge of project controls, scheduling, budgeting, cost management, and construction administration.
Experience reviewing design documents, construction drawings, specifications, schedules, and other technical documentation.
Experience supporting public-sector, municipal, or other large capital construction programs.
Strong written and verbal communication, coordination, and stakeholder management skills.

Familiarity with school operations, stakeholder engagement, phased construction, summer acceleration projects, and occupancy constraints in active educational environments.
Experience coordinating with government agencies, permitting authorities, regulatory agencies, and utility providers.

Demonstrated ability to manage multiple concurrent projects and priorities within a large capital portfolio.

Manage multiple projects throughout the full project lifecycle, from planning and design through construction, closeout, and occupancy
