new_jobs.title: Deputy Program Manager (Contingency)
new_jobs.description:
Title

Deputy Program Manager (Contingency)

Belong, Connect, Grow, with KBR!

Program Summary

KBR’s Exploration & Logistics (E&L) business unit delivers mission-critical solutions supporting global defense, federal civilian, logistics, engineering, and space exploration missions. E&L provides integrated capabilities across logistics and sustainment, mission operations, engineering services, readiness and modernization programs, scientific research support, and exploration initiatives in some of the world’s most complex and challenging environments.

The business unit supports customers across the Department of Defense, federal civilian agencies, and commercial partners, delivering innovative solutions that enhance mission readiness, operational effectiveness, and long-term mission success.

Job Summary

The Deputy Program Manager (DPM) serves as the principal deputy to the Program Manager and provides direct support in the execution, oversight, and management of all contract performance under the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) Public Assistance Technical Assistance Contract (PA TAC VI). The DPM assists in providing leadership, operational direction, quality management, and administrative oversight to ensure the successful delivery of technical, programmatic, and administrative support services in support of FEMA's Public Assistance Program and disaster recovery mission.

The DPM supports the planning, organization, coordination, and execution of all contract activities, resources, personnel, subcontractors, and deliverables while ensuring compliance with contract requirements, FEMA policies, federal regulations, and applicable performance standards. The DPM helps manage a geographically dispersed workforce supporting multiple concurrent disasters nationwide and contributes to rapid mobilization, scalable operations, and continuous mission readiness.

The DPM serves as the designated alternate to the Program Manager and assumes responsibility for program operations during the Program Manager's absence. This position requires the ability to support nationwide disaster operations, including periodic travel and availability during emergency activation periods.

The DPM assists with day-to-day contract execution across all task orders and disaster assignments, supporting nationwide surge operations and disaster deployment activities. Responsibilities include coordinating staffing, resource allocation, deployment readiness, and workload balancing to support multiple simultaneous disaster operations. The DPM ensures timely mobilization, deployment, tracking, and demobilization of personnel and must possess demonstrated experience supporting FEMA programs or similarly complex federal programs.

The DPM supports the Program Manager in ensuring contract performance meets or exceeds all performance metrics, service level requirements, and quality standards. The DPM contributes to program governance activities, including performance assessments, risk management, quality reviews, corrective action implementation, and continuous improvement initiatives while supporting overall cost, schedule, and performance objectives.

This role requires an experienced, adaptable leader capable of operating in austere and rapidly changing environments while maintaining strict compliance with contractual, safety, and quality standards. The DPM will promote KBR's Zero Harm culture and ensure operations are executed in accordance with company policies, applicable regulations, and customer requirements.

Please Note:
This role is contingent upon final project approval and contract funding.

Core Competencies

Program Leadership and Team Management
Federal Program and Project Management
FEMA Public Assistance Expertise
Disaster Recovery Operations
Stakeholder Engagement
Quality Assurance and Continuous Improvement
Risk Management
Workforce Planning and Resource Coordination
Contract Administration
Financial and Schedule Management
Strategic Communications
Problem Solving and Decision Making
Mission-Focused Service Delivery

The Deputy Program Manager Shall Demonstrate

Comprehensive knowledge of FEMA Public Assistance Program delivery, grant management, and disaster recovery operations.
Experience applying Stafford Act authorities, 2 CFR Part 200, FEMA Public Assistance Program and Policy Guide (PAPPG), and applicable federal regulations.
Experience supporting large-scale disaster recovery operations involving multiple simultaneous federally declared disasters.
Training and experience in Incident Command System (ICS) principles and emergency management operations.
Experience overseeing geographically dispersed teams supporting field, regional, and headquarters operations.
Familiarity with FEMA's recovery mission, state, local, tribal, and territorial coordination processes, and stakeholder engagement practices.
Demonstrated ability to support program management functions including workforce management, deployment operations, risk mitigation, and performance monitoring.

Roles And Responsibilities

Serve as the primary deputy to the Program Manager and act on behalf of the Program Manager when designated.
Support day-to-day execution of the contract and associated task orders, ensuring strategic objectives, performance goals, financial targets, and customer expectations are achieved.
Coordinate with FEMA leadership, Contracting Officer Representatives (CORs), task order managers, subcontractors, and stakeholders to facilitate successful contract performance.
Monitor operational performance, identify risks and issues, and implement corrective actions to maintain program effectiveness.
Support surge staffing activities, including workforce planning, deployment coordination, personnel tracking, and resource allocation.
Assist in managing geographically dispersed personnel and ensuring adequate staffing levels across disaster operations.
Lead or support program reviews, readiness assessments, executive briefings, and performance monitoring activities.
Support implementation of quality management processes and continuous improvement initiatives.
Assist in managing program schedules, budgets, deliverables, subcontractor performance, and contract compliance requirements.
Prepare reports, metrics, dashboards, and executive-level briefings regarding program status, performance, risks, and mitigation strategies.
Ensure compliance with FEMA guidance, contractual requirements, federal regulations, cybersecurity requirements, records management policies, and privacy standards.
Maintain close coordination with program leadership to ensure continuity of operations across all contract activities.
Support customer engagement efforts and maintain positive working relationships with FEMA and other key stakeholders.
Promote employee development, safety awareness, teamwork, and operational excellence throughout the program.

Highly Desired Training

FEMA National Incident Management System (NIMS)

IS-100: Introduction to Incident Command System (ICS)
IS-200: Basic Incident Command System for Initial Response
IS-700: National Incident Management System, An Introduction
IS-800: National Response Framework, An Introduction

FEMA Public Assistance Training

IS-634: Introduction to FEMA Public Assistance Program
IS-1000: Public Assistance Program Eligibility
IS-1001: Public Assistance Project Formulation
IS-1002: Public Assistance Damage Assessment and Cost Estimating
IS-1004: Public Assistance Grants Portal Training
FEMA Public Assistance Program and Policy Guide (PAPPG) training

Additional FEMA-Required Training

FEMA cybersecurity and information security awareness training
FEMA privacy and Personally Identifiable Information (PII) protection training
FEMA records management training
Ethics and procurement integrity training, as applicable
Annual FEMA-mandated refresher training

Preferred Certifications

The following certifications are highly desirable:

Project Management Professional (PMP)
Certified Emergency Manager (CEM)
Associate Emergency Manager (AEM)
FEMA Professional Development Series (PDS)
FEMA Advanced Professional Series (APS)
Lean Six Sigma Green Belt or Black Belt
Certified Construction Manager (CCM)
Professional Engineer (PE)
Certified Floodplain Manager (CFM)
PMI Risk Management Professional (PMI-RMP)

Continuing Education Requirements

The Deputy Program Manager shall maintain all required professional certifications and complete FEMA-required training throughout the life of the contract.

The DPM Shall

Complete all mandatory FEMA onboarding and security training within 30 days of assignment.
Maintain annual cybersecurity, privacy, records management, and ethics certifications as required by FEMA.
Complete FEMA policy update training within 60 days of issuance of new or revised guidance.
Participate in FEMA readiness exercises, disaster workforce development activities, and program-specific training events.
Maintain certification renewals in accordance with issuing organization requirements and provide verification upon request.

Basic Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Business Administration, Emergency Management, Public Administration, Engineering, Construction Management, Program Management, or a related field.
Minimum of ten (10) years of progressively responsible experience supporting federal programs, disaster recovery operations, or emergency management programs.
Minimum of five (5) years of experience in a leadership role supporting program, project, or operations management functions on federal contracts of similar scope and complexity.
Demonstrated experience supporting FEMA programs, disaster recovery missions, or similar federal emergency management operations.
Knowledge of FEMA Public Assistance processes, grant management, and disaster recovery operations.
Strong leadership, organizational, and team-building skills.
Expertise in KPI reporting, risk management, performance monitoring, and change management processes.
Excellent written, verbal, and presentation communication skills.
Strong analytical, problem-solving, conflict resolution, and decision-making abilities.
Ability to manage multiple priorities and work effectively in high-tempo operational environments.
U.S. citizenship.
Ability to travel and deploy nationwide in support of disaster response and recovery operations.

Preferred Qualifications

Master's degree in Business Administration, Emergency Management, Public Administration, Engineering, or related field.
PMP certification.
Certified Emergency Manager (CEM) certification.
FEMA Professional Development Series (PDS) completion.
Experience supporting PA TAC, IA TAC, HMGP, or other FEMA recovery contracts.
Experience managing subcontractors and geographically dispersed teams.
Familiarity with FEMA Grants Manager and Grants Portal systems.
Experience supporting large-scale disaster recovery operations involving multiple simultaneous disasters.
Strong proficiency with reporting tools, performance dashboards, data analytics, and executive briefings.

Belong, Connect and Grow at KBR

At KBR, we are passionate about our people and our Zero Harm culture. These inform all that we do and are at the heart of our commitment to, and ongoing journey toward being a People First company. That commitment is central to our team of team’s philosophy and fosters an environment where everyone can Belong, Connect and Grow. We Deliver – Together.

SOVOS

Enterprise Project Manager

Managed & Professional Services·Full-Time·UK/AMS/ESP

Build Your Future With Us

The digitization of tax compliance is fundamentally changing global commerce and how businesses need to operate and grow. Governments now have real-time visibility into business data, creating new challenges and new opportunities for organizations around the world. At Sovos, we're transforming tax compliance from a business requirement into a driver of growth through AI-powered technology that delivers the accurate, real-time insights businesses need to make smarter decisions.

We're solving more than today's tax compliance challenges. We're helping reshape global economies by enabling organizations to navigate increasingly complex and rapidly changing regulatory environments with confidence – and helping communities thrive.

AI is accelerating what's possible, enabling tax and technology professionals to more effectively drive critical regulatory decisions. That's where Sovos excels, combining intelligent technology with human expertise to help customers stay ahead of change.

Don't worry if you don't check every box. We're focused on hiring great people, not perfect resumes. It's less about what you've done elsewhere and more about what you're capable of doing here.

The Role

At Sovos, we're transforming how global enterprises navigate regulatory complexity. We're looking for an Enterprise Project Manager to join our European Professional Services team, with the ability to be based in the United Kingdom, Netherlands, or Spain. This is a senior delivery role for an experienced PM who understands the complexity of enterprise SaaS implementations and brings deep familiarity with tax compliance, e-invoicing, or regulatory technology. You'll own end-to-end delivery of complex, multi-country implementations for enterprise clients across EMEA, operating with a high degree of autonomy and directly impacting client satisfaction and the reputation of Sovos Professional Services in Europe.

More Specifically, You Will

Own end-to-end project delivery for enterprise e-invoicing and tax compliance implementations across multiple EMEA countries simultaneously.
Serve as the primary point of contact and escalation for client stakeholders, from project teams to C-suite sponsors, throughout the engagement lifecycle.
Develop and maintain detailed project plans, risk registers, issue logs, and status reports; proactively surface risks and drive resolution before they become escalations.
Lead structured project governance, including weekly status meetings, monthly steering committee sessions, and go/no-go decision processes, in alignment with Sovos delivery methodology.
Manage project scope rigorously; identify, document, and drive change orders when client requests exceed agreed SOW boundaries.
Coordinate cross-functional Sovos resources (Solution Consultants, Technical Consultants, SAP specialists, Regulatory, and Product teams) to deliver against project commitments.
Track and report project hours against PS retainer balances; proactively communicate burn-down status and initiate retainer expansion conversations at appropriate thresholds.
Leverage AI-assisted project management tools to improve delivery efficiency, automate status reporting, and surface risk patterns across the client portfolio.
Manage Hypercare periods post-go-live and execute formal project handover to Sovos Customer Support.
Contribute to the continuous improvement of PS delivery methodology, SOW templates, onboarding playbooks, and project governance frameworks.

What You Bring to Sovos

You've built solid experience delivering enterprise SaaS implementations in a client-facing Professional Services environment, with demonstrated expertise managing complex, multi-stakeholder implementations in the tax compliance, e-invoicing, VAT, or regulatory technology space.
Demonstrated success managing projects with enterprise clients (500M+ revenue) across multiple countries and time zones concurrently.
Experience with SAP-integrated implementations (SAP ECC, S/4HANA, or Process Orchestration) is strongly preferred.
Hands-on experience with retainer-based PS engagements, including scope management, change order discipline, and hour burn-down governance.
Familiarity with EMEA e-invoicing mandates, including France (PPF/PDP), Germany (XRechnung/Peppol), Poland (KSeF), and/or Turkey (e-Fatura/e-Arşiv), is a significant advantage.
Exceptional stakeholder management skills: able to build trust with client executives and navigate competing priorities without losing delivery momentum.
Solid commercial acumen: you understand the relationship between project delivery, revenue recognition, and margin, and manage accordingly.
Proactive risk management mindset: you identify and escalate issues early, document decisions, and drive accountability without being asked.
Clear, structured communicator (written and verbal) capable of adapting tone and detail level for technical teams, client project managers, and executive sponsors alike.
Comfortable operating with ambiguity and driving clarity in fast-moving, multi-mandate environments where priorities can shift quickly.
Proficiency with project management tooling (e.g. Cloud Coach, Salesforce, Jira, or equivalent PSA/CRM platforms); comfort with AI-assisted workflows to enhance delivery speed and insight generation is a plus.
Demonstrated project management capability through certifications (e.g., PMP, PRINCE2) or equivalent proven delivery experience is valued.
Equivalent experience to a Bachelor's degree in Business, Information Systems, Finance, or a related field.
Fluency in English required; proficiency in French, German, Dutch, Spanish, or Polish is a meaningful advantage given the client base.
Due to client contractual obligations, the successful candidate will be asked to clear a background check upon hire.

Referment is working with a fast-growing technology company providing software to charities, community organisations and public sector customers.

They're looking for a Customer Implementation Manager to take ownership of new client onboarding and help customers successfully adopt the platform.

This is a hands-on role combining implementation, customer success, project management and process improvement. You'll work with multiple customers simultaneously, taking them from initial kick-off through to successful launch and ongoing adoption.

The customer base is varied and often non-technical, so the ability to understand problems, explain technology simply and build strong relationships is just as important as traditional SaaS experience.

The Role

Customer Onboarding & Implementation

Owning customer implementations from kick-off through to go-live.
Managing multiple concurrent client projects and priorities.
Breaking complex implementations into clear, manageable phases.
Setting timelines and managing customer expectations.
Understanding how customers currently operate and helping them translate their requirements into effective use of the platform.
Training users with varying levels of technical confidence.
Helping customers adopt new functionality and get increasing value from the product.
Identifying issues that genuinely affect implementation and prioritising them appropriately.
Supporting data migrations and other technical aspects of onboarding.
Visiting customers where required to understand how they work in practice.

Customer Operations & Process Improvement

Improve and standardise the customer onboarding process as the company grows.
Build documentation, guides and repeatable processes.
Help manage customer support and resolve issues.
Identify opportunities to automate repetitive work.
Track customer feedback and feature requests.
Work closely with the product and engineering teams to communicate customer priorities.
Identify patterns across customer feedback and turn them into useful product insights.
Help develop scalable customer success processes as the customer base expands.

What We're Looking For

You could already be working within Customer Success, Implementation, Onboarding or Professional Services, but we're equally interested in people who have developed the right skills elsewhere.

Relevant Backgrounds Could Include

Customer implementation or onboarding.
Customer success.
Project or programme management.
Consulting

What's more important is that you can demonstrate:

Excellent customer communication and relationship-building skills.
The ability to manage several projects and competing priorities simultaneously.
Confidence working with customers who aren't particularly technical.
The ability to teach people how to use new systems clearly and patiently.
Strong problem-solving skills and the confidence to challenge a customer's proposed solution when necessary.
A structured approach to project delivery.
The ability to turn recurring work into documented and scalable processes.
Good judgement around prioritisation and urgency.
Comfort working within a fast-moving and changing environment

Experience working with charities, community organisations or the public sector would be particularly valuable.

Technical experience, especially around data migrations, SaaS platforms, customer data or integrations, would also be useful but isn't essential.

This could suit a Customer Success Manager, Implementation Manager, Customer Onboarding Manager, Implementation Consultant or Project Manager, as well as someone looking to move into technology from another client-facing environment.

new_jobs.description:
Why Harvey

At Harvey, we’re transforming how legal and professional services operate. By combining frontier agentic AI, an enterprise-grade platform, and deep domain expertise, we’re reshaping how critical knowledge work gets done for decades to come.

This is a rare chance to help build a generational company at a true inflection point. We have strong product-market fit and world-class investor support. We’re scaling fast and defining a new category in real time. The work is ambitious, the bar is high, and the opportunity for growth — personal, professional, and financial — is unmatched.

Our team moves fast, takes ownership, and is deeply committed to the mission — operating with intensity, staying close to our customers, and pushing each other for excellence. We live by three values: Decisiveness, Simplicity, and Job's Not Finished. We act quickly on clear judgment over perfect information, we believe simplicity is what scales, and we're never satisfied with where we are. If you want to do the best work of your career alongside people who share that drive, we'd love to build with you.

At Harvey, the future of professional services is being written today — and we’re just getting started.

Role Overview

People Operations is taking on more complex, cross-functional program work as Harvey grows globally — from opening new entities and markets, to integrating acquisitions, to evolving the systems and providers that support our employees around the world. These programs span People, Finance, Legal, Tax, IT, and other teams, and need a dedicated owner who can bring the whole thing together.

You’ll run point on these initiatives end-to-end: defining requirements, building the plan, driving decisions and execution across teams, and making sure we’re ready to go live. This is a hands-on program management role — you’ll work closely with functional experts, but you’re expected to get into the substance, develop a point of view, and personally execute work wherever needed to drive the program forward.

What You'll Do

Own complex global programs from scope through go-live and handoff, including new entity formation and geographic expansion, M&A integrations, and the ongoing evolution of our infrastructure in existing markets — such as EOR and vendor transitions, payroll migrations, and other major operational changes.
Build and drive the program plan, translating a messy objective into clear requirements, workstreams, owners, dependencies, readiness gates, and decisions; proactively surface risks, resolve blockers, and adjust the plan as facts change.
Connect the dots across functions. Partner deeply with People Ops, People Systems, Finance, Payroll, Legal, Tax, IT, and other teams to understand how decisions in one workstream affect another and make sure nothing falls between the cracks.
Own program communication and change management, from crisp executive updates and decision points to clear, thoughtful communications for employees affected by a change.
Build repeatable infrastructure as we scale, turning what we learn from each program into better templates, SOPs, playbooks, and operating processes for the next one.
Keep the employee experience at the center. Make sure operational complexity behind the scenes translates into a coordinated, thoughtful experience for employees — particularly during high-change moments like entering a new market, transitioning employment infrastructure, or integrating an acquired team.

What You Have

7+ years of experience leading complex, cross-functional programs, with experience in global People infrastructure such as geographic expansion, entity formation, M&A integration, or related work.
A hands-on operating style and strong bias toward action. You dig into the substance, step into gaps, and do what’s needed to keep complex work moving. You’re comfortable figuring things out as you go and have good judgment about what requires deeper diligence versus what simply needs to get done.
Strong stakeholder management and judgment, with the ability to align specialists and senior leaders across functions without formal authority.
Clear, direct executive communication. You can distill a complicated program into the decisions, risks, and tradeoffs that matter and communicate them appropriately to everyone from executives to affected employees.
Strong AI fluency. You use AI as a core part of how you work — to move faster, synthesize information, work through ambiguity, and increase the quality and leverage of your output.

Compensation

$120,000 - $200,000 USD

new_jobs.title: Senior Technical Program Manager
new_jobs.description:
Who We Are

Bidgely (which means "electricity" in Hindi) is a Vertical AI company built for the utility industry, delivering appliance-level intelligence for every customer, grid asset, and hour of the year through our UtilityAI™ Platform. We're accelerating a clean energy future by giving utilities and their customers the ability to make smarter, data-driven energy decisions.

Bidgely's platform is connected to 38M+ meters across 45+ utility deployments and is backed by over 20 patents. Our approach combines patented disaggregation science, generative AI for natural-language insight, and agentic AI for autonomous operations — giving utilities a level of individual-customer intelligence and grid insights that horizontal AI and legacy analytics platforms can't match.

Bidgely has been named #7 in Applied AI on Fast Company's list of Most Innovative Companies in the World and recognized as a Utility Analytics Leader by Guidehouse.

What We Do

Powered by our unique patented technology, Bidgely's UtilityAI™ Platform transforms multiple dimensions of utility data — such as energy consumption, demographics, and customer interactions — into deeply accurate and actionable consumer energy insights. We leverage these insights to empower each customer with personalized recommendations tailored to their individual personality and lifestyle, usage attributes, behavioral patterns, purchase propensity and beyond.

The same technology that powers Bidgely's customer suite also enables a set of powerful grid applications. From a distributed energy resources (DER) and grid edge perspective, Bidgely is accelerating utility innovation with data-driven solutions for solar PVs, electric vehicle (EV) detection, EV behavioral load shifting and managed charging, load forecasting, grid analytics, and rate designs. Bidgely's UtilityAI™ energy analytics platform provides deep visibility into generation and consumption for better peak load shaping and grid planning and delivers targeted recommendations for new value-added products and services.

How You Fit In

The Senior Technical Program Manager (STPM) owns Bidgely's largest and most technically and commercially complex utility engagements, combining the roles of technical consultant, functional consultant, and project manager. The STPM also acts as a delivery and practice leader for the broader Customer Onboarding team. The STPM works closely with a dedicated delivery team on the technical build, with R&D and Product Management on platform direction, and with Systems Integrator partners on multi-party engagements — while owning the customer relationship, executive stakeholder management, and program outcomes. The STPM reports into the Director, Customer Onboarding and is part of Bidgely's Customer Onboarding team.

Core responsibilities span the following areas:

Project Management

Be the face of Bidgely for the customer during the implementation phase, owning the relationship, and being an advocate for them internally
Manage Bidgely's largest and most complex utility implementations end to end from Onboarding to Launch, leading cross-functional teams across Delivery, Engineering, Product, and Sales
Oversee project financials — including cost tracking, budget, and margin — for assigned engagements
Contribute to contract reviews for new deals and change orders
Represent the Onboarding team in sales presentations as needed
Develop and apply a deep understanding of energy markets and customer behaviors to help Bidgely customers take full advantage of the technology

Technology Implementation

Own the overall solution design and development for Bidgely's most complex utility customers, working with our global engineering team — including requirement analysis, customer journey scope discussion, data integration, design, solution architecture, implementation, delivery, and customer-facing technical issue resolution
Be the product expert who collaborates with utility customers to understand requirements, map them to product features, and finalize product customizations and changes
Manage project deliverables, ensuring on-time, high-quality delivery through a hands-on approach
Produce technical and product documents that clearly define customer requirements and solution design in collaboration with the customer's IT and business teams
Partner with Bidgely R&D and Product Management to design new platform functionality and implementation tooling, informed by patterns observed across the most complex customer implementations

Practice Leadership

Mentor and provide delivery and technical guidance to colleagues
Own executive-level customer relationships for high-visibility engagements
Develop proposals and statements of work for new and expanding engagements
Identify and help scope account expansion opportunities during delivery
Represent Customer Onboarding in quarterly business reviews (QBRs)
Work with Systems Integrator (SI) partners to plan and execute complex, multi-party implementations
Train Bidgely, SI, and customer teams on Bidgely's project methodology and product capabilities
Develop internal tools and processes that improve delivery quality and reduce implementation timelines
Support hiring and interviewing for the broader TPM team

Skills And Qualifications

Required Qualifications

7-11 years of software integration project experience at a SaaS company, or experience in a top-tier systems integration consulting firm and/or delivering enterprise solutions at a fast-paced start-up
Track record of successfully delivering complex, cross-functional implementations for large, high-touch enterprise customers, ideally with ACV of $500K+
Experience as the primary point of contact for enterprise customers, including designing and deploying solution architecture in a customer-facing role
Experience working with globally dispersed customers and teams
Experience with Agile software development methodologies and cloud-based B2B implementations
Comfortable creating and tracking project plans, risks, and status reports via Wrike, Smartsheets, Jira, or similar cloud project management tools
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with excellent written and verbal communication and the ability to translate complex technical issues for non-technical stakeholders
Demonstrated ability to mentor and develop less experienced team members
Highly organized, collaborative, and proactive, with a customer-first mentality

Preferred Qualifications

Working knowledge of SQL, Python, REST APIs, or data transformation tools, with a hands-on aptitude for applying them directly
Passion for or experience within the energy or energy efficiency sector
PMP certification

What You Get

Growth Potential: Build your career at a fast-scaling company at the forefront of AI-driven energy innovation
Collaborative Environment: Work with a passionate team united by the goal of a clean energy future
Leading Technology: Gain hands-on exposure to the AI, machine learning, and data platforms shaping the future of the utility industry

Benefits

Medical, Dental, and Vision insurance from day one
HSA, FSA, and DCFSA plans
401(k) plan
Flexible paid time off
Annual wellness stipend
Annual professional development stipend
Paid parental leave
Mental health and wellness resources for you and your family

Other Perks

Employee Discounts: Preferred pricing on entertainment, technology, and insurance products
Mentorship: Access to mentorship from experienced industry leaders
Flexible Work Arrangements: Remote-friendly scheduling built around how you work best
Community Service Days: Paid time to volunteer for causes you care about

Location

Remote within the US with up to 15% travel

Salary And Compensation

The base salary ranges from $135,000-$160,000 DOE. This role may also be eligible for a discretionary annual bonus and equity, subject to company policy and role level.

In accordance with the California Equal Pay and Pay Transparency laws, the approximate annual base compensation range is listed above. The actual offer, reflecting the total compensation package and benefits, will be determined by a number of factors including the applicant's experience, knowledge, skills, and abilities, as well as internal equity among our team.

Diversity, Equity, Inclusion and Equal Opportunity

At Bidgely we're on a mission to make a difference and build a workplace where every unique voice is heard and celebrated. Here, we believe that celebrating the unique backgrounds, perspectives and abilities of every employee makes an impact not only for our company internally but also for our clients, customers and community.

We are an equal opportunity employer and believe that the inclusive atmosphere we build together will enable every person to grow, contribute and thrive. Our hiring decisions are based on your skills, talent, and passion – not on your background, gender, race, age, or the quirky way you dance at office parties.

The Program Manager plays a key role in managing the K12 School Playbook process, analyzing implementation and performance information, identifying trends and effective practices across schools, and supporting the development and adoption of scalable academic solutions. Millennium Space Systems

Millennium Space Systems, a part of Boeing Defense, Space and Security (BDS), is a fast, agile small satellite company focused on national security space. Our missions have direct impact to global security, like missile warning and Earth observation.

Our team is curious, bold and innovative. We take risks, innovate and explore new techniques and technologies. We influence change because we challenge the status quo. And when we watch our satellites launch, we know each one of us made it happen.

Job Summary:
This position is responsible for creating a secure environment to facilitate the successful development and execution of classified programs at the assigned organization where classified information is stored, accessed, or where accessed personnel are assigned.

The Industrial Security Manager will enforce strict adherence to applicable laws as well as national DoD, and other security policies and requirements. Coordination of classified matters with the respective government representatives will be at the forefront of their responsibilities. The Industrial Security Specialist will be charged with the establishment of quality training for assigned accessed personnel and conduct and document annual compliance inspections and develop Corrective Action Plans (CAP). This is an onsite role in our office in El Segundo, CA.

This position’s internal job code is Industrial Security Specialist. Our team is currently hiring for a level K.

Position Responsibilities

Manages the Program Security Team while ensuring compliance for security requirements for Collateral, SCI and SAP programs while providing technical expertise concerning all security disciplines; evaluate and deliver performance reviews
Oversee successful support of staff assisted visits, security reviews and inspections as well as conducting initial, recurring and refresher security education training
Oversee process of accreditation of facilities; ensure maintenance of accreditation artifacts for all facilities, ensure accreditations are accurate and current
Reviews Contract Data Requirements List (CDRL) deliverables for security. This includes but is not limited to IS & Physical Security Plans, Management Plans and Test Plans. Provide comments and recommendations as required
Assists with the development of Program Protection Implementation Plans (PPIP); Review and provide comments for Statements of Work, contracts, Request for Proposal (RFP), and various Security Plans
Develops and maintains Standard Operating Procedures (SOP) that adhere to government policy and regulations. Additionally, craft policies that telegraph procedures for operations at the company level

Boeing First-Line Leader Assessment:
To be considered for this position you will be required to complete an assessment as part of the selection process. Failure to complete the assessment will remove you from consideration.

Basic Qualifications (Required Skills/Experience)

Minimum of 10 years’ experience in Industrial Security
Must have experience with SAPs
Must be knowledgeable of the following Government policies; NISPOM, DoDM 5205.07 ICD-705, Sensitive Compartmented Information Facilities (ICD/ICS 705 compliance documents), DoD 5105.21 Vol 1-3, Sensitive Compartmented Information Security Manual Series, The Security, Use and Dissemination of Sensitive Compartmented Information, JSIG
Minimum of 1 year managing and developing high performing teams supporting Industrial Security management
This position requires an active U.S. Top Secret Security Clearance with SCI Eligibility (U.S. Citizenship Required. A U.S. Security Clearance that has been active in the past 24 months is considered active)

Preferred Qualifications (Desired Skills/Experience)

Experience with successful support of staff assisted visits, security reviews and compliance inspections
Experience with generating DD-254s and sub-contractor oversight
Experience with physical construction of Special Access Program Facilities (SAPFs) and/or Sensitive Compartmented Information Facilities (SCIFs); ICD-705 knowledge
OPSEC & Program Protection Planning experience

others to transfer documentation, schedules, and other information.

Why Harvey

At Harvey, we’re transforming how legal and professional services operate. By combining frontier agentic AI, an enterprise-grade platform, and deep domain expertise, we’re reshaping how critical knowledge work gets done for decades to come.

This is a rare chance to help build a generational company at a true inflection point. We have strong product-market fit and world-class investor support. We’re scaling fast and defining a new category in real time. The work is ambitious, the bar is high, and the opportunity for growth — personal, professional, and financial — is unmatched.

Our team moves fast, takes ownership, and is deeply committed to the mission — operating with intensity, staying close to our customers, and pushing each other for excellence. We live by three values: Decisiveness, Simplicity, and Job's Not Finished. We act quickly on clear judgment over perfect information, we believe simplicity is what scales, and we're never satisfied with where we are. If you want to do the best work of your career alongside people who share that drive, we'd love to build with you.

At Harvey, the future of professional services is being written today — and we’re just getting started.

Role Overview

People Operations is taking on more complex, cross-functional program work as Harvey grows globally — from opening new entities and markets, to integrating acquisitions, to evolving the systems and providers that support our employees around the world. These programs span People, Finance, Legal, Tax, IT, and other teams, and need a dedicated owner who can bring the whole thing together.

You’ll run point on these initiatives end-to-end: defining requirements, building the plan, driving decisions and execution across teams, and making sure we’re ready to go live. This is a hands-on program management role — you’ll work closely with functional experts, but you’re expected to get into the substance, develop a point of view, and personally execute work wherever needed to drive the program forward.

What You'll Do

Own complex global programs from scope through go-live and handoff, including new entity formation and geographic expansion, M&A integrations, and the ongoing evolution of our infrastructure in existing markets — such as EOR and vendor transitions, payroll migrations, and other major operational changes.
Build and drive the program plan, translating a messy objective into clear requirements, workstreams, owners, dependencies, readiness gates, and decisions; proactively surface risks, resolve blockers, and adjust the plan as facts change.
Connect the dots across functions. Partner deeply with People Ops, People Systems, Finance, Payroll, Legal, Tax, IT, and other teams to understand how decisions in one workstream affect another and make sure nothing falls between the cracks.
Own program communication and change management, from crisp executive updates and decision points to clear, thoughtful communications for employees affected by a change.
Build repeatable infrastructure as we scale, turning what we learn from each program into better templates, SOPs, playbooks, and operating processes for the next one.
Keep the employee experience at the center. Make sure operational complexity behind the scenes translates into a coordinated, thoughtful experience for employees — particularly during high-change moments like entering a new market, transitioning employment infrastructure, or integrating an acquired team.

What You Have

7+ years of experience leading complex, cross-functional programs, with experience in global People infrastructure such as geographic expansion, entity formation, M&A integration, or related work.
A hands-on operating style and strong bias toward action. You dig into the substance, step into gaps, and do what’s needed to keep complex work moving. You’re comfortable figuring things out as you go and have good judgment about what requires deeper diligence versus what simply needs to get done.
Strong stakeholder management and judgment, with the ability to align specialists and senior leaders across functions without formal authority.
Clear, direct executive communication. You can distill a complicated program into the decisions, risks, and tradeoffs that matter and communicate them appropriately to everyone from executives to affected employees.
Strong AI fluency. You use AI as a core part of how you work — to move faster, synthesize information, work through ambiguity, and increase the quality and leverage of your output.

In most companies, research demand far exceeds supply. Time, cost, and lack of access to expertise hold teams back. In today’s AI-powered world, anyone can build a product fast. The real challenge? Deeply understanding user needs and building the right product. That’s where Maze comes in.

We believe companies shouldn’t have to choose between building fast and building right. Maze makes research accessible, intuitive, and fast so product teams can put user insights at the center of every decision.

Our platform enables researchers, designers, and product managers to quickly recruit participants, run studies autonomously, and surface insights that actually drive product decisions. Our AI capabilities automate the busywork and add depth and direction to the insights themselves.

That’s why Maze was recently named the #1 user research platform
in UX Tools’ Design Tools Survey—and why we’re scaling fast across industries like B2B SaaS, e-Commerce, Financial Services, Retail, and Automotive, supporting world class customers such as Uber, Amazon, Atlassian, Anthropic & more.

Maze is a Series B
company backed by top-tier investors (Felicis, Emergence & Amplify). We operate a global remote workforce driven by our core values.

We’re looking for a Research Operations Program Manager
to help build and scale our research recruitment operations at Maze.

In this role, you’ll work with prospects, customers, and partners to help our users recruit the right participants for their studies. You’ll sit at the center of our research
participant marketplace
, where customers come to Maze with recruitment needs and we fulfill them through our network of panel partners.

You’ll play an important role in delivering a great experience for our customers while helping shape the processes, tools, and strategy behind our growing recruitment business.

As a Research Operations Manager at Maze, you will:

Own relationships with our panel vendors, assessing performance across quality and fulfillment to determine how we prioritize and route orders.
Onboard new panel vendors based on business needs, including running due diligence to ensure quality and compatibility.
Review and interpret customer recruitment requirements and assess feasibility.
Place and manage orders across our network of panel vendors.
Monitor order progress and fulfillment, proactively identifying and flagging issues or delays.
Troubleshoot common fulfillment challenges, including low incidence rates and screener drop-off, and escalate when needed.
Build end-to-end processes that improve the efficiency and scalability of our operating model.
Partner with Product and Engineering to help shape and build the internal tools that support our operations.
Bring operational insights into decisions around our product roadmap and pricing.
Develop customer-facing materials that make our recruitment offering easy to understand and use.
Take on additional areas of ownership as the business grows, based on your strengths and interests.

You should apply if:

You have 3+ years of experience in operations, consulting, research operations, UX research, or market research.
You’ve worked in fast paced, ambiguous environments and have experience taking projects from strategy through implementation.
You’re scrappy and resourceful, and comfortable figuring things out as you go.
You have strong attention to detail and can manage multiple moving pieces without losing sight of the customer experience.
You’re a strong collaborator who can work effectively with a wide range of internal and external stakeholders and keep projects moving forward.
You’re an exceptional communicator who can deliver recommendations clearly and concisely to customers.
You’re comfortable presenting to both technical and executive audiences, whether through presentations, demos, or more informal discussions.
You’re a high-energy team player with a strong track record of building collaborative relationships across an organization.

Nice to have:

Experience working at a high-growth B2B SaaS company.
Experience in Market Research or UX Research.
Experience working in a remote environment.

Inclusivity and Pay

At Maze, we are dedicated to building an equitable, inclusive, and authentic workspace. Unique and diverse perspectives are welcomed, and continuous growth is encouraged. We believe that people are more than their resumes, so if your past experience looks different than the criteria listed, we'd still love to hear from you. We appreciate and celebrate non-traditional life routes and encourage you to apply should you connect with a job description or the Maze culture.

Maze values transparency and it enables us to approach compensation equitably across the world. We are informed by data and regularly check our salary ranges (either United States or Rest of World) against other venture backed companies. Additionally, we are proud of our holistic and generous benefits offerings, included in every compensation package.

Your salary is dependent upon many factors, including years of experience, expertise, etc. During your first interview, you can expect to have an open conversation with your recruiter regarding your compensation expectations.

Why Maze is unique

Early-stage startup: You will join an early-stage startup with less than 150 team members. This means you'll have the unique opportunity to directly impact success and help shape the future of Maze.
Market disruption: We believe that the way companies build products is fundamentally broken and the user research market is ripe for disruption. For too long, companies have been forced to choose between rapid development without user insights or investing months into research before bringing products to market. But there's finally a groundswell building around a path forward that eliminates this compromise - and Maze is leading the charge.
Product-market Fit: Maze is used by 100,000+ brands across 4,000 companies, from SMB to enterprises, and in the last fiscal year, we saw 6.5M questions answered, supporting 25K decisions

Health insurance with international coverage, vision, and dental: 100% of the team member premium paid
For some locations, coverage options vary, please see our benefits pages for more information

Flexible work schedule where you manage your own working hours
Monthly Bonus.ly points that are awarded to others to recognize teamwork, dedication and helpfulness - points can be cashed out for gift cards and more

new_jobs.description:
This position is accountable and responsible for managing from complex Prefab Customer project orders

to exceed customer expectations through project execution. This includes initiating, planning, executing,

controlling, and closing of customer projects (Customer Project Process).

Individual in this position confirms and manage customer project to deliver an Integrated Package scope

of work including, and not limited to Electrical Enclosures (e-Houses) with electrical distribution and

automation control systems, HAVC and fire and gas systems, plus additional customer features and

services. Manages complete job process from order preparation, thru manufacturing release, product

shipment, post shipment support and financial reconciliation utilizing a base knowledge of Schneider

Electric products and processes.

Takes ownership for validating the project’s scope of work, schedule, cost, and contract terms with the customer, including, risks, technical and commercial elements and becomes lead contact for customer during project execution. (Project Initiation).
Develops and maintain project organization, schedule, risk register and communicates with the customer to ensure expectations are being met. Direct engagement with the customer internal manufacturing facilities and third-party vendors. (Project Planning).
Monitor the execution of the customer’s project order, verifying execution of the project through kick-off meetings, project schedule, communication to all parties and exchange of technical requirements and project plan information. Manage decision making process towards the best cross-functional compromise and effectiveness. Drives Risk and Change Managements, solves problems with customer interaction that results in positive feedback and improved relationship. (Project Execution)
Lead the monitor and control of the performance of the customer’s project through its lifecycle. Key activities include task completion verification, project team monitoring, managing the exchange of project updates across the project team members, schedule reporting, issue resolution, and contract administration. Monitor project progress against the plan and establish regular reports to key stakeholders. Measure and reports project performance indicators (Monitor and Control Project Work)
Lead the closeout of the customer’s project to include financial reconciliation, verification of job site equipment arrival, installation and start-up coordination, and training support completion. Point of Contact with the customer, and coordination with support services such as field services, after-shipment support, and training functions. Captures lessons learn and documentation approvals for future projects. (Project Close)
Utilizes a base knowledge of Schneider Electric products and their use and demonstrates an understanding of the fundamental knowledge, processes and terminology needed for effective project management

Excellent communication skills (written and verbal), including the ability to understand complex technical topics
Strong leadership skills including, team leading, employee mentoring and development, and the ability to empower others through delegating responsibility.
Strong interpersonal skills with a desire to work in a team environment
Proven organizational and time/project management skills
Advanced understanding of project management and project finance
Ability to build and maintain technical and commercial awareness
Ability to define and put in place short and medium term action plans to increase customer satisfaction while improving business growth and efficiency
Strong organization, planning and customer service skills
Proficient in Microsoft Office programs including but not limited to, Word, Project, and Excel
Results oriented, critical thinking and problem-solving skills
Influence and convince skills
Decision-making and escalate appropriately when arbitration is required.

Conflict management & Stress tolerance
Adaptability

Four-year degree required

PMP (PMI), CPMP/CPMA SE Internal Certification preferred

Understanding of systems integration, HVAC or other building or electronic control systems is a plus

BJC is hiring for a Project Manager. Ideal candidate will have experience in Clinical Engineering. Previous Healthcare industry experience is a must. This is a hybrid role.

Overview

BJC HealthCare
is one of the largest nonprofit health care organizations in the United States, delivering services to residents primarily in the greater St. Louis, southern Illinois and southeast Missouri regions. With net revenues of $6.3 billion and more than 30,000 employees, BJC serves patients and their families in urban, suburban and rural communities through its 14 hospitals and multiple community health locations. Services include inpatient and outpatient care, primary care, community health and wellness, workplace health, home health, community mental health, rehabilitation, long-term care and hospice.

BJC is the largest provider of charity care, unreimbursed care and community benefits in the state of Missouri. BJC and its hospitals and health service organizations provide $785.9 million annually in community benefit. That includes $410.6 million in charity care and other financial assistance to patients to ensure medical care regardless of their ability to pay. In addition, BJC provides additional community benefits through commitments to research, emergency preparedness, regional health care safety net services, health literacy, community outreach and community health programs and regional economic development.

BJC’s patients have access to the latest advances in medical science and technology through a formal affiliation between Barnes-Jewish Hospital and St. Louis Children’s Hospital with the renowned Washington University School of Medicine, which consistently ranks among the top medical schools in the country.

In Clinical Engineering our mission is to provide a team of empowered professionals providing continued improvement in patient care and equipment planning & support technologies. About the Opportunity

The organization is the trusted source for open source. By delivering hardened, secure, and production-ready builds of all the open source software engineers and AI agents rely on, the company helps organizations build faster, stay compliant, and eliminate risk.

The company's security organization sits at the intersection of proactive, long-term initiatives and reactive, business-critical work. As the organization has grown, managing that balance, anticipating the downstream impact of changing priorities, and giving leadership a clear view of security risk and exposure have become increasingly important, and increasingly complex.

This role is seeking a Senior Technical Program Manager to bring structure and visibility to this space.

The individual will operate horizontally across the security organization, partnering with Product Security, Cyber Resiliency, and Governance & Trust. While they will be closely embedded with those teams in their day-to-day work, they will also help coordinate priorities, dependencies, and execution across the broader security organization.

The impact of this role will extend well beyond security. Because security intersects with nearly every function at the company — including engineering, product, legal, finance, sales, and marketing — the individual will build the systems, processes, and relationships that enable effective collaboration across the company.

This is a senior, strategic role with substantial room to grow. The individual will not inherit a fully defined playbook; they will help create it. They will establish the processes, dashboards, and prioritization mechanisms that give the security organization greater clarity and leverage, and over time, expand that impact into broader company-wide programs and operating processes.

Key Responsibilities

Own workflow, project tracking, and dependency management across the three security teams, making it clear what’s on track, what’s at risk, and what downstream impact changes may have.
Build and maintain dashboards and reporting that give company leadership a clear, durable view of security risk, exposure, and program health.
Partner closely with the primary security team on day-to-day execution while supporting the other two teams as priorities and capacity allow.
Make and communicate prioritization decisions when demand exceeds the security organization’s capacity — including finding alternatives and helping stakeholders understand trade-offs, rather than simply saying no.
Design and implement lightweight processes that help security teams operate more effectively without creating unnecessary overhead for engineers.
Work directly with product, engineering, and other partner teams to establish clear, effective ways of working with security.
As the role grows, extend impact beyond security by helping shape broader company processes, including how the organization approaches planning, prioritization, and cross-functional execution.

Required Qualifications

5+ years of experience in program management, technical program management, or operations roles
Meaningful experience in a broad, cross-functional operations or program management role, supporting many stakeholders across an organization rather than working within a single, self-contained team.
Security experience is a plus, but not required. More important is the ability to operate effectively in a horizontal role with a large and diverse stakeholder group.
A track record of building processes and exercising sound judgment in ambiguous environments, rather than defaulting to standard frameworks or playbooks.
Strong stakeholder management skills, with the ability to act as a strategic and consultative partner across functions.
Experience managing competing priorities and communicating trade-offs, including difficult prioritization decisions, clearly and thoughtfully.
Comfort working in a fast-moving, scaling environment where processes are still being built and refined.

Additional Information

Security work at the company doesn’t follow a predictable schedule. Proactive initiatives and reactive, business-critical needs are constantly competing for the same time and attention. This role exists to bring structure to that tension — helping the security organization make deliberate choices about where to focus and how to respond when priorities inevitably shift.

At the same time, company leadership needs a clearer, more consistent view of the security posture, risk, and exposure than there is currently a dedicated mechanism to provide. The individual will build that reporting infrastructure and make it durable as the organization grows.

And because security intersects with nearly every part of the business, there will be an unusually broad view of how the company operates. Over time, there will be the opportunity to take what is learned in security and apply it to larger, org-wide programs and processes — helping shape not just how security works, but how the company works as a whole.

Base Salary Range

$153,000—$180,000 USD

About Us

The organization lives and breathes its company values:

Customer obsessed — Focus on delivering solutions to customers that create value and make their lives better.
Bias for intentional action — Prioritize, plan, try things, and fail fast.
Don't take ourselves too seriously (but we do serious work) — Solving an important problem which takes focus, but also enjoying the journey.
Trust each other and assume good intentions — Transparent with decisions to empower team members to make well informed decisions.

A few of the benefits offered:
Flexible & Remote-First Culture:
Work remotely with team meetup opportunities, bi-annual destination summits, and a monthly stipend for coworking spaces, phone and internet costs.

Reporting to the Director, Compliance & Ethics, this role has full programmatic accountability for the development, implementation, oversight, and continuous improvement of the company’s program to protect quantum customer confidential information, manage appropriate access and personnel safeguards, and support consistent execution of customer commitments across the quantum foundry business. This role serves as the company’s subject matter expert on program administration and partners closely with Legal and business partners to align the program with customer commitments, applicable laws (including antitrust laws), and internal policies. The Senior Manager partners closely with the Director to ensure the program is well-designed, effectively implemented, and supports SkyWater’s ability to remain a trusted multi-customer quantum foundry.

Responsibilities

Quantum Foundry Customer Assurance Program Management

Develop and maintain program policies, procedures, and guidance documents. Collaborate with cross functional partners to drive execution, implementation and adherence to such policies.
Establish and manage governance structures, including any necessary steering committees and working groups, and serve as the senior functional authority on program matters escalated from across the business. Ensure escalations are risk reviewed, cataloged, and elevated to the Director as necessary to appropriately govern the program.
Coordinate implementation and monitoring of program requirements across business functions, including customer information safeguards, system access, personnel assignments, and consistent application of customer commitments and service-level practices, taking into account contractual terms, paid service levels, technical requirements, and business priorities.
Implement, own, and advance a mature, well-documented program that is risk-based, operationally effective, and defensible to customers and external stakeholders.
Develop and maintain program dashboards, key performance indicators and any required reporting, including reporting to the Director, executive leadership, and external parties as appropriate.
Lead program activities. Create a repository of program requirements and an inventory control framework to track activities.
Administer information safeguards and access-control requirements, including tracking non-disclosure agreements, system access, information flows, roster status, and employee assignments by customer; support personnel changes and serve as the primary operational point of contact for program requirements and inquiries.

Training & Communications

Lead the design and execution of awareness campaigns and communications, including support for customer-facing materials describing SkyWater’s safeguards and program commitments; tailor messaging by audience and risk exposure; maintain records of training delivery and completion to support internal oversight, customer assurance, and audit or regulatory needs.

Risk Assessment & Monitoring

Develop monitoring and testing activities to assess program effectiveness across the organization.

Remediation & Continuous Improvement

Investigations & Incident Management

new_jobs.title: Technical Project Manager III - Lunar Permanence
new_jobs.description:
Application Close Date

Applications will be accepted on an ongoing basis until the requisition is closed.

At Blue Origin, we envision millions of people living and working in space for the benefit of Earth. We’re working to develop reusable, safe, and low-cost space vehicles and systems within a culture of safety, collaboration, and inclusion. Join our team of problem solvers as we add new chapters to the history of spaceflight! 

This role is part of the Lunar Permanence business unit, which develops Blue Origin’s Blue Moon landers and related products. To further Blue Origin's mission of millions of people living and working in space for the benefit of Earth, we are building sustainable infrastructure for our transport of crew and cargo from Earth to the lunar surface.

As part of a hardworking team of engineering professionals, you will use your technical expertise, leadership skills, and commitment to quality to positively impact safe human spaceflight. A passion for our mission and vision is required. If you're excited about providing near-term value, solving novel problems, learning about interesting topics, and taking on challenging work, we encourage you to apply.

This role reports to the RF Systems Group within the Lunar Permanence business unit. As part of a growing, hardworking, and curious team of design engineers, you'll work directly with NASA and our National Team Partners on the Human Landing System (HLS) Sustaining Lunar Development (SLD) program. You will play a key role in developing the Lunar Permanence system that will return humans to the Moon and extend human presence permanently beyond Earth.

Special Mentions

Relocation provided
Travel up to 10% of the time
Interviews will include a technical assessment

Responsibilities Include But Are Not Limited To

Lead technical project management for RF component development projects supporting Blue Origin's Lunar Vehicles.
Apply expertise in project management, technical product maturation, and organizational development to create efficient, cost-effective solutions for the Lunar landers.
Support the RF Systems team in developing and maintaining technical, cost, and schedule baselines.
Prepare for and support program reviews, including those with Lunar Permanence Senior Management.
Help establish and maintain the Lunar vehicle meeting and review operating rhythm.
Develop robust plans to meet deliverables and manage key operating metrics, including technical performance, cost, schedule, and risk.
Contribute to RF Systems product roadmaps, including the development and integration of technologies to meet program milestones and future derivatives.
Partner with internal and external customers to understand and shape current and future mission needs.
Interface with external vendors and suppliers to manage RF hardware procurement, development schedules, and technical compliance.
Provide high-caliber technical leadership by coordinating with the RF Systems Director, IPTs, and supporting Blue Origin business units.
Monitor technical progress, budget, schedule, deliverables, and risks; recommend changes to Lunar RF Systems and Vehicle Directors as needed.
Communicate progress to leadership through program management reviews, finance reviews, long-term forecasting, and project deep dives.
Apply sound engineering and business judgment to ensure products are efficiently designed, manufactured, procured, tested, qualified, and delivered.
Support Agile-based planning and execution.
Collaborate with other RF Systems Technical Project Managers to establish best practices and streamline processes across IPTs.

Minimum Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Electrical, Mechanical, Aerospace, or a related Engineering field.
5+ years of experience in engineering operations related to avionics/electronics new product introduction.
Experience with MS Project and Jira.
Experience with design/build/test project methodology, including critical path scheduling, IMP/IMS, risk management, requirements management, and Cost Account Management.
Strong team leadership and people management skills.
Proven ability to build trust and maintain positive, professional relationships.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills.

Preferred Qualifications

MBA or Master's degree in Electrical Engineering or a related engineering/scientific field.
Experience with space hardware procurement and supplier management.
Experience with Earned Value Management (EVM).
Experience with flight hardware development and qualification.
Experience with Confluence and Primavera P6.

Base Pay Range For

CA applicants is $130,706.00 - $182,987.70 CO applicants is $119,814.00 - $167,738.55 WA applicants is $130,706.00 - $182,987.70 VA applicants is $130,706.00 - $182,987.70

Other Site Ranges May Differ

Culture Statement

Don’t meet all desired requirements? Studies have shown that some people are less likely to apply to jobs unless they meet every single desired qualification. At Blue Origin, we are dedicated to building an authentic workplace, so if you’re excited about this role but your past experience doesn’t align perfectly with every desired qualification in the job description, we encourage you to apply anyway. You may be just the right candidate for this or other roles.

Export Control Regulations

Applicants for employment at Blue Origin must be a U.S. citizen or national, U.S. permanent resident (i.e. current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum.

Background Check

Required for all positions: Blue’s Standard Background Check
Required for Certain Job Profiles: Defense Biometric Identification System (DBIDS) background check if at any time the role requires one to be on a military installation
Required for Certain Job Profiles: Drivers who operate Commercial Motor Vehicles with a Gross Vehicle Weight (GVW), Gross Vehicle Weight Rating (GVWR) or combination of power unit and trailer that meets or exceeds 10,001 lbs. and/or transports placardable amounts of hazardous materials by ground in any vehicle on a public road while in commerce, may be subject to additional Federal Motor Carrier Safety Regulations including: Driver Qualification Files, Medical Certification (obtained before onboarding), Road Test, Hours of Service, Drug and Alcohol Testing, vehicle inspection requirements, CDL requirements (if applicable) and hazardous materials transportation/shipping training.
Required for certain Job Profiles: Ability to obtain and maintain Merchant Mariner Credential, which includes pre-employment and random drug testing as well as DOT physical

Benefits

Benefits include: Medical, dental, vision, basic and supplemental life insurance, paid parental leave, short and long-term disability, 401(k) with a company match of up to 5%, and an Education Support Program.
Stock Options for all regular employees (working at least 20 hours/week)
Paid Time Off: Up to four (4) weeks per year based on weekly scheduled hours, and up to 14 company-paid holidays.
Dependent on role type and job level, employees may be eligible for benefits and bonuses based on the company's intent to reward individual contributions and enable them to share in the company's results, or other factors at the company's sole discretion. Bonus amounts and eligibility are not guaranteed and subject to change and cancellation. Please check with your recruiter for more details.

Equal Employment Opportunity

Blue Origin is proud to be an Equal Opportunity/Affirmative Action Employer and is committed to attracting, retaining, and developing a highly qualified and dedicated work force. Blue Origin hires and promotes people on the basis of their qualifications, performance, and abilities. We support the establishment and maintenance of a workplace that fosters trust, equality, and teamwork. We provide all qualified applicants for employment and employees with equal opportunities for hire, promotion, and other terms and conditions of employment, regardless of their race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin/ethnicity, age, physical or mental disability, genetic factors, military/veteran status, or any other status or characteristic protected by federal, state, and/or local law. Blue Origin will consider for employment qualified applicants with criminal histories in a manner consistent with applicable federal, state, and local laws, including the Washington Fair Chance Act, the California Fair Chance Act, the Los Angeles Fair Chance in Hiring Ordinance, and other applicable laws. For more information on “Know Your Rights,” please see here.

🌍 우리는 누구인가

“우리는 깨끗한 책상 위에서만 일하지 않는다.
우리는 시스템을 만든다.
쓰레기장이라도 가서, 현장을 본다.
그릿은 버티는 힘이고, VWS 정신은 바꾸는 힘이다.”
VWS는 직무(Job)
가 아닌 미션(Mission)
으로 움직입니다.
우리는 스스로 문제를 찾아내고, 현장에서 답을 만들며, 그 답을 시스템으로 고정하는 사람들을 원합니다.
Zero-to-One Builder
는 현장에서 손을 더럽히고, 시스템으로 회사를 확장시키는 Mission Owner
입니다.

CEO Thinking

VWS는 결과로 움직이는 팀입니다.

우리는 보고서가 아닌 시스템으로 문제를 해결하고, 그 시스템을 만든 사람에게 자본과 지분의 권리를 부여합니다.
경쟁하지 않고, 경쟁에서 벗어나며, 남들이 하지 않는 선택으로 시장을 새로 설계합니다.
모든 일은 Why → What → KPI → ROI 로 역산하며, 목적과 숫자가 없는 일은 하지 않습니다.

개발을 이해하는 기획자, 데이터를 읽는 디자이너, 비즈니스를 보는 엔지니어처럼요.

결국 제로투원형 인재란, 아직 검증되지 않은 가치를 먼저 알아보고 스스로 증명할 수 있는 사람입니다.
“남들이 인정하지 않은 가치를 먼저 알아보는 눈이 희소성을 만든다.”

AI/데이터 기반으로 프로세스 자동화
결과를 측정하고, 개선의 루프 설계

⚙️ 이런 사람을 찾습니다

“직무가 아니라, 문제로 움직이는 사람.”
